{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_6f6a548d740249f6a1413a8ab778f270",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/PM-80421-hosted-api-capability-prioritization-acceptance-rollout.json",
    "title": "Hosted API: Capability Prioritization, Acceptance Matrix, and Rollout Constraints",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"PM-80421\",\n  \"team\": \"product-management\",\n  \"title\": \"Hosted API: Capability Prioritization, Acceptance Matrix, and Rollout Constraints\",\n  \"status\": \"In Review\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-02-12\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2025-02-20\",\n  \"creator\": \"Sofia Patel\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Marcus Rivera\",\n  \"project\": \"Hosted API Stabilization\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2025-W07\",\n  \"estimate\": \"8\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2025-03-14\",\n  \"release\": \"hosted-api-2025.03\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"true\",\n  \"customer_impact\": \"medium\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"api\",\n    \"launch\",\n    \"hosted\",\n    \"chat\",\n    \"embeddings\",\n    \"rerank\",\n    \"acceptance\"\n  ],\n  \"summary\": \"Define prioritized scope, explicit acceptance criteria, and a conservative rollout plan for chat, completions, embeddings and rerank hosted endpoints with clear gating metrics and operational runbooks.\",\n  \"background\": \"Redwood needs a single coordinated PRD that sets a prioritized subset of hosted API features for the next public launch window. Multiple product docs exist focusing on surface design, but there is inconsistent acceptance criteria between teams which risks divergent rollout readiness and customer confusion. This ticket consolidates decisions, defines measurable acceptance gates, and produces a launch checklist that can be followed by PM, Eng, Design, and Support.\",\n  \"goals\": [\n    \"Agree on a minimum viable capability set for public hosted API launch across chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank\",\n    \"Produce an acceptance matrix with pass/fail gating metrics for functional, performance, and security requirements\",\n    \"Define a staged rollout plan (canary -> regional scaling -> general availability) with rollback conditions\",\n    \"Deliver an actionable launch checklist and handoff artifacts for support, docs, and partner teams\"\n  ],\n  \"non_goals\": [\n    \"Shipping dedicated or private deployment bundles (separate project)\",\n    \"Complete SDK language parity for all non-core SDKs\\u2014we will ship core JS/Python first\",\n    \"Large scale model training or onboarding of new architectures\\u2014this is focused on serving and surface stability\"\n  ],\n  \"product_requirements\": [\n    \"Endpoint coverage: chat, completions, embeddings (single and batched), rerank (server-side) must be exposed via REST + OpenAPI spec\",\n    \"API contract stability: response schemas must be versioned and backward compatible unless a major version bump is announced\",\n    \"Authentication: OAuth2 and API keys supported; SSO/SAML enterprise flow documented and validated in private tests\",\n    \"Structured output: function/tool-calling primitives available on chat endpoints with schema validation hooks\",\n    \"Batching & latency knobs: server-side batching must be configurable per-route; default config must meet SLO targets\",\n    \"Quotas & rate limiting: tier-aware defaults + per-customer overrides; error responses must include retry-after headers where applicable\"\n  ],\n  \"endpoint_specific_requirements\": [\n    \"Chat: streaming (chunked) responses, SSE support in REST, conversation state token included for KV cache affinity\",\n    \"Completions: single-turn responses, max_tokens enforcement, temperature/top_p controls, stopping sequences honored\",\n    \"Embeddings: deterministic outputs for same model+input+params; support both single and up-to-8-batch endpoints; embedding dimensionality documented\",\n    \"Rerank: accept candidate lists up to configured max, return score per candidate and stable ranking semantics; provide opt-out for full-text features for privacy-conscious customers\"\n  ],\n  \"performance_slos\": [\n    \"99th percentile latency for completions (1k tokens) <= 300ms for cached/short sequences under hosted free-tier load profile\",\n    \"Median generation latency for chat (stream resume) <= 150ms per chunk for standard models\",\n    \"Embeddings throughput target: 500 qps per shard with p95 latency <= 70ms for single input\",\n    \"Availability SLO: 99.9% regional during GA for core endpoints (excludes scheduled maintenance)\"\n  ],\n  \"telemetry_and_observability\": [\n    \"Per-route token-level cost and latency metrics in Console\",\n    \"Tracing hooks for request lifecycle (ingress -> model -> response stream) with sampling at document.title: Hosted API: Capability Prioritization, Acceptance Matrix, and Rollout Constraints
document.content:
{
  "key": "PM-80421",
  "team": "product-management",
  "title": "Hosted API: Capability Prioritization, Acceptance Matrix, and Rollout Constraints",
  "status": "In Review",
  "priority": "P1",
  "created_at": "2025-02-12",
  "updated_at": "2025-02-20",
  "creator": "Sofia Patel",
  "assignee": "Marcus Rivera",
  "project": "Hosted API Stabilization",
  "cycle": "2025-W07",
  "estimate": "8",
  "due_date": "2025-03-14",
  "release": "hosted-api-2025.03",
  "security_review_required": "true",
  "customer_impact": "medium",
  "labels": [
    "api",
    "launch",
    "hosted",
    "chat",
    "embeddings",
    "rerank",
    "acceptance"
  ],
  "summary": "Define prioritized scope, explicit acceptance criteria, and a conservative rollout plan for chat, completions, embeddings and rerank hosted endpoints with clear gating metrics and operational runbooks.",
  "background": "Redwood needs a single coordinated PRD that sets a prioritized subset of hosted API features for the next public launch window. Multiple product docs exist focusing on surface design, but there is inconsistent acceptance criteria between teams which risks divergent rollout readiness and customer confusion. This ticket consolidates decisions, defines measurable acceptance gates, and produces a launch checklist that can be followed by PM, Eng, Design, and Support.",
  "goals": [
    "Agree on a minimum viable capability set for public hosted API launch across chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank",
    "Produce an acceptance matrix with pass/fail gating metrics for functional, performance, and security requirements",
    "Define a staged rollout plan (canary -> regional scaling -> general availability) with rollback conditions",
    "Deliver an actionable launch checklist and handoff artifacts for support, docs, and partner teams"
  ],
  "non_goals": [
    "Shipping dedicated or private deployment bundles (separate project)",
    "Complete SDK language parity for all non-core SDKs\u2014we will ship core JS/Python first",
    "Large scale model training or onboarding of new architectures\u2014this is focused on serving and surface stability"
  ],
  "product_requirements": [
    "Endpoint coverage: chat, completions, embeddings (single and batched), rerank (server-side) must be exposed via REST + OpenAPI spec",
    "API contract stability: response schemas must be versioned and backward compatible unless a major version bump is announced",
    "Authentication: OAuth2 and API keys supported; SSO/SAML enterprise flow documented and validated in private tests",
    "Structured output: function/tool-calling primitives available on chat endpoints with schema validation hooks",
    "Batching & latency knobs: server-side batching must be configurable per-route; default config must meet SLO targets",
    "Quotas & rate limiting: tier-aware defaults + per-customer overrides; error responses must include retry-after headers where applicable"
  ],
  "endpoint_specific_requirements": [
    "Chat: streaming (chunked) responses, SSE support in REST, conversation state token included for KV cache affinity",
    "Completions: single-turn responses, max_tokens enforcement, temperature/top_p controls, stopping sequences honored",
    "Embeddings: deterministic outputs for same model+input+params; support both single and up-to-8-batch endpoints; embedding dimensionality documented",
    "Rerank: accept candidate lists up to configured max, return score per candidate and stable ranking semantics; provide opt-out for full-text features for privacy-conscious customers"
  ],
  "performance_slos": [
    "99th percentile latency for completions (1k tokens) <= 300ms for cached/short sequences under hosted free-tier load profile",
    "Median generation latency for chat (stream resume) <= 150ms per chunk for standard models",
    "Embeddings throughput target: 500 qps per shard with p95 latency <= 70ms for single input",
    "Availability SLO: 99.9% regional during GA for core endpoints (excludes scheduled maintenance)"
  ],
  "telemetry_and_observability": [
    "Per-route token-level cost and latency metrics in Console",
    "Tracing hooks for request lifecycle (ingress -> model -> response stream) with sampling at 10%",
    "Failure classification: distinguish client error, quota, model OOMs, runtime backpressure, and network errors",
    "Alerting: burn rate alerts for error spikes and latency regressions with documented on-call escalation path"
  ],
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "API: OpenAPI spec file committed and published; example requests + SDK snippets for JS/Python included",
    "Compatibility: backward compatibility test suite green across 3 prior minor revisions for response schemas",
    "Performance: load test for target customer profile executed and p95/p99 metrics within SLO budget",
    "Security: threat model review completed and critical/major findings remediated; KMS integration tested end-to-end",
    "Reliability: automated canary pipeline validates new model binary for 72h at canary traffic with zero severity incidents",
    "Docs: Console docs and quickstarts published; migration guide for customers with earlier endpoint variants",
    "Support readiness: runbook (incident + FAQ) authored and triaged with L2 and L3 on-call; training session held"
  ],
  "rollout_plan": [
    "Phase 0 - Internal Staging: Burn-in with internal teams and partner beta customers for 2 weeks",
    "Phase 1 - Canary (5% traffic): Route small percentage of production traffic; monitor canary-specific metrics and automated rollback windows",
    "Phase 2 - Regional Expansion (50% region): Open to more customers in region, enable quotas and limits enforcement",
    "Phase 3 - GA (100%): Full exposure worldwide with pricing and quota tiers; start marketing motion"
  ],
  "canary_metrics_and_gates": [
    "Error rate delta > 0.5% absolute compared to baseline -> automatic rollback",
    "Latency p95 regression > 30% vs baseline -> hold promotion and trigger perf triage",
    "Client-facing correctness failures (schema mismatch, missing fields) > 0 in canary logs -> fail promotion",
    "Cost burn rate > 150% of predicted budget for canary segment -> pause and investigate caching/batching settings"
  ],
  "launch_checklist": [
    "Finalize API surface and freeze non-breaking changes",
    "Sign-off from Security on pen-test and KMS integration",
    "Ops runbooks published (on-call, escalation, rollback) and verified via tabletop exercise",
    "Console dashboards for tokens/cost/latency per route are live and pre-populated with synthetic traffic",
    "SDK release candidates (JS/Python) published with migration notes",
    "Billing & quotas pipelines connected and validated end-to-end with test customer accounts",
    "Support FAQ and primary triage playbook published in Knowledge Base",
    "Multi-region deployment validated and health checks automated"
  ],
  "migration_and_deprecation_strategy": [
    "Provide explicit deprecation timeline for legacy endpoint variants with automated translation layer for 6 months",
    "Offer opt-in compatibility headers for customers who need strict legacy behaviour",
    "Measure adoption and provide targeted outreach for top 50 customers before hard deprecation"
  ],
  "risks_and_mitigations": [
    "Risk: Model OOMs at tail causing request failures -> Mitigation: reserve fallback model variant with lower memory profile and graceful degradation",
    "Risk: Schema changes break downstream SDKs -> Mitigation: strict schema validation in CI + backwards compatibility test harness",
    "Risk: Cost overruns from unbounded batching -> Mitigation: default per-route throttles + billing alerts",
    "Risk: Entitlement or quota misconfig leads to customer impact -> Mitigation: staged rollout with quota enforcement and explicit billing tests"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "Runtime team: batching and KV cache toggles must be available via route config",
    "Console: dashboards and rollout controls implemented and tested",
    "SDK: JS and Python clients with new API surface and streaming primitives",
    "Security: SSO/SAML and KMS integration completion",
    "Legal/Billing: pricing tiers agreed and billing pipeline tested"
  ],
  "stakeholders": [
    "PM: Sofia Patel",
    "Eng (Runtime): Priya Natarajan",
    "Eng (API): Marcus Rivera",
    "Design: Leo Martinez",
    "Security: Hannah Kim",
    "Support: Anika Shah",
    "Sales: Daniel Ortiz"
  ],
  "open_decisions": [
    "Final verb names for streaming endpoints (stream vs SSE vs chunked) \u2014 decision needed by 2025-02-25",
    "Default batching window (20ms vs 40ms) \u2014 leaning 20ms but waiting perf test results",
    "Embeddings batch size max: 8 or 16 \u2014 impact analysis in progress"
  ],
  "links": [
    "Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/hosted-api/acceptance-matrix",
    "OpenAPI: https://api.redwood.ai/specs/hosted-api-2025-03.yaml",
    "Design mockups: https://drive.redwood.ai/design/hosted-api-console-rollout",
    "Load tests: https://perf.redwood.ai/reports/hosted-api-canary-2025-02",
    "PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/8153"
  ],
  "comments": [
    "2025-02-13 Sofia Patel: Initial draft posted; asked runtime and API leads for input on batching knobs.",
    "2025-02-15 Marcus Rivera: Added definitive API contract section and requested OpenAPI generation from API infra team.",
    "2025-02-17 Priya Natarajan: Raised concern about default caching affinity for chat; proposed 'conversation_token' header to improve KV hit rate.",
    "2025-02-18 Hannah Kim: Security review scheduled for 2025-02-21; noted KMS integration needs test fixture for key rotation",
    "2025-02-20 Design sign-off: Leo Martinez reviewed console flows; requested explicit error states for streaming interruptions"
  ],

    "title": "API Family Delivery Specification: chat/completions/embeddings/rerank — requirements, scope changes, and launch rundown",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"PM-51555\",\n  \"team\": \"product-management\",\n  \"title\": \"API Family Delivery Specification: chat/completions/embeddings/rerank \\u2014 requirements, scope changes, and launch rundown\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-02-18\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2025-03-05\",\n  \"creator\": \"Aisha Patel\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Marcus Lee\",\n  \"project\": \"Hosted API unification\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2025-W10\",\n  \"estimate\": \"8\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2025-03-20\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"hosted-api\",\n    \"chat\",\n    \"embeddings\",\n    \"rerank\",\n    \"launch\",\n    \"acceptance\"\n  ],\n  \"parent_issue\": [\n    \"PM-20984\",\n    \"PM-27581\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-39012\",\n    \"ENG-40211\",\n    \"ENG-41820\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"high\",\n  \"release\": \"hosted-api-2025.03\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"true\",\n  \"description\": \"This ticket is the canonical PRD and launch readiness checklist for the hosted API family delivering chat, completions, embeddings, and a rerank capability as a cohesive surface. It consolidates functional requirements, clarified scope after recent trade-offs, measurable acceptance criteria, and a sequenced launch checklist with canary/rollout guidance. Goal: ship a single, predictable API suite that supports developer-friendly defaults, per-endpoint SLAs, cost-control knobs (batching/kv caching), and a clear rollback path. This doc focuses on the delivery contract for hosted customers and handoff items for Dedicated/Private as needed.\",\n  \"requirements\": [\n    \"Unified API surface: single /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings endpoints with explicit type param for chat/completion mode and an opt-in rerank route; backward-compatible aliases maintained for legacy clients.\",\n    \"SDK parity: JS/Python SDKs expose identical method signatures, streaming support for chat & completions, and a high-level rerank helper that accepts candidate lists and returns ranked ids with scores.\",\n    \"Performance targets: P50 token latency < 70ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) on hosted S1 models; P95 < 200ms. Embeddings: P99 < 150ms for 1-4 inputs. Rerank throughput: support 2500 candidate evaluations/sec per allocation.\",\n    \"Reliability: 99.95% availability for hosted endpoints with automatic fallback to smaller model variants when capacity or quota limits are hit.\",\n    \"Cost controls: default server-side batching enabled for multi-request workloads, configurable batching window per API key, and documentation of cost/latency tradeoffs.\",\n    \"Security & privacy: all requests logged with token-level cost metadata; customer data in hosted mode retained for 30 days by default with opt-out. KMS integration required for dedicated/private integrations (see ENG dependency).\",\n    \"Observability: per-route dashboards, request sampling for traces, per-key token cost breakdowns, and regression alerts tied to evaluation prompt sets.\",\n    \"Acceptance test harness: end-to-end test suites in CI that validate correctness for deterministic prompts, streaming order integrity, and rerank stability on seeding datasets.\",\n    \"Rollout controls: canary targeting by API key, region, and plan with automatic rollback on defined SLO regressions.\"\n  ],\n  \"out_of_scope\": [\n    \"Self-hosted deployment packaging \\u2014 Private/Dedicated install artifacts are handled in a separate project; this ticket only defines API contracts for compatibility.\",\n    \"Custom model fine-tuning pipeline \\u2014 not part of hosted endpoint initial launch, will be considered post-MVP.\",\n    \"Language-specific SDKs beyond JS/Python for initial launch (Go/Rust scheduled in next cycle).\"\n  ],\n  \"scope_changes\": [\n    \"2025-02-20: Removed inline synchronous rerank from /v1/generate path \\u2014 introduced dedicated /v1/rerank endpoint to simplify latency SLAs and caching semantics. Decision: improves isolation of compute patterns and enables separate autoscaling.\",\n    \"2025-02-27: Deferred multi-tenant per-request KV-cache pinning to post-launch due to runtime integration complexity (moved to ENG-41820).\",\n    \"2025-03-03: Reduced streaming window default from 250ms to 100ms after QA latency regressions; added explicit SDK opt-in for 'aggressiveStreaming' to avoid surprising cost changes for low-volume users.\"\n  ],\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": [\n    \"API contract: OpenAPI spec published and validated by SDK generation tooling; no breaking changes vs agreed alias mappings.\",\n    \"Performance: Verified in staging with production-like traffic that P50 and P95 latency targets are met for the S1 model family across regions (benchmarks attached).\",\n    \"Stability: End-to-end error rate < 0.5% during a 24-hour stability run with randomized prompt corpus; no data loss on streaming connections longer than 30s.\",\n    \"Security: KMS integration smoke test green and data-retention config enforced for hosted accounts; security review signoff received.\",\n    \"Observability: Dashboards and regression alerts configured; alert playbooks documented and reviewed by on-call rotation.\",\n    \"Docs & SDKs: Public docs (API reference, migration guide, cost guidance) published; JS/Python SDKs have release candidates and integration tests pass.\",\n    \"Rollout: Canary passes defined SLO gates for 72 hours before extending to 50% of traffic; automated rollback works end-to-end.\"\n  ],\n  \"launch_checklist\": [\n    \"Finalize OpenAPI and example payloads (docs) \\u2014 owner: Docs team \\u2014 status: todo\",\n    \"SDK release RC1 (JS/Python) with streaming and rerank helpers \\u2014 owner: SDK team (ENG-39012) \\u2014 status: in progress\",\n    \"Staging perf run and benchmark report \\u2014 owner: Performance eng \\u2014 status: in progress\",\n    \"Security review & KMS test \\u2014 owner: Security \\u2014 status: todo\",\n    \"Billing integration for token accounting and plan enforcement \\u2014 owner: Billing eng \\u2014 status: todo\",\n    \"Canary config created (per-key targeting) and automation jobs defined \\u2014 owner: Infra \\u2014 status: todo\",\n    \"E2E CI suite passes with randomized prompt sets including rerank fidelity checks \\u2014 owner: QA \\u2014 status: todo\",\n    \"Create rollback playbook and automate fallback to compact-model variant \\u2014 owner: SRE \\u2014 status: todo\",\n    \"Customer comms draft (changelog + migration guidance) \\u2014 owner: Growth/PM \\u2014 status: todo\",\n    \"Post-launch monitoring dashboard and 24/72h escalations staffing plan \\u2014 owner: Observability \\u2014 status: todo\"\n  ],\n  \"rollout_plan\": \"Week 0: internal dogfooding and integration tests. Week 1: 1% canary (internal + selected customers) for 72h with automated SLO monitoring. Week 2: extend to 25% if canary healthy, monitor cost signals; enable additional regions. Week 3: broad rollout to GA if acceptance gates hold. At every step, feature flags allow disabling streaming or rerank. Rollback path documented to redirect traffic to legacy endpoint aliases and smaller model family.\",\n  \"qa_notes\": [\n    \"Create deterministic seed corpus (1k prompts) that includes streaming edge cases and long-running completions.\",\n    \"Include fuzzing for rerank inputs (duplicate IDs, empty candidate lists, malformed scores).\",\n    \"Validate SDK streaming order using sequence IDs and simulate flaky network conditions.\",\n    \"Run cost smoke tests to ensure batching does not cause token overcount regressions.\"\n  ],\n  \"review_comments\": [\n    \"Marcus Lee (ENG): 'Agree with splitting rerank to dedicated route \\u2014 simplifies autoscaler and lowers tail-latency risk.' \\u2014 2025-02-20\",\n    \"Sofia Nguyen (Design): 'Docs need quick-start examples that show cost tradeoffs \\u2014 add a 3-step migration snippet.' \\u2014 2025-02-22\",\n    \"Priya Desai (Security): 'KMS integration needs an explicit end-to-end test in CI; flagging as required for release.' \\u2014 2025-02-25\",\n    \"Ben Carter (PM): 'We should gate GA on billing integration; otherwise customers will hit unexpected charges.' \\u2014 2025-03-01\"\n  ],\n  \"links\": [\n    \"https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PI/API+Family+Spec+2025\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/412\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/988\",\n    \"https://dashboard.redwood.ai/d/hosted-api/perf-benchmarks?orgId=1\",\n    \"https://docs.redwood.ai/reference/migration-guides/api-family-2025\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"requirements\",\n    \"out_of_scope\",\n    \"scope_changes\",\n    \"acceptance_criteria\",\n    \"launch_checklist\",\n    \"rollout_plan\",\n    \"qa_notes\",\n    \"review_comments\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_ada92facaa334d3688c6a8371e0d001a\"\n}",

document.content:
{
  "key": "PM-51555",
  "team": "product-management",
  "title": "API Family Delivery Specification: chat/completions/embeddings/rerank \u2014 requirements, scope changes, and launch rundown",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P1",
  "created_at": "2025-02-18",
  "updated_at": "2025-03-05",
  "creator": "Aisha Patel",
  "assignee": "Marcus Lee",
  "project": "Hosted API unification",
  "cycle": "2025-W10",
  "estimate": "8",
  "due_date": "2025-03-20",
  "labels": [
    "hosted-api",
    "chat",
    "embeddings",
    "rerank",
    "launch",
    "acceptance"
  ],
  "parent_issue": [
    "PM-20984",
    "PM-27581"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-39012",
    "ENG-40211",
    "ENG-41820"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "high",
  "release": "hosted-api-2025.03",
  "security_review_required": "true",
  "description": "This ticket is the canonical PRD and launch readiness checklist for the hosted API family delivering chat, completions, embeddings, and a rerank capability as a cohesive surface. It consolidates functional requirements, clarified scope after recent trade-offs, measurable acceptance criteria, and a sequenced launch checklist with canary/rollout guidance. Goal: ship a single, predictable API suite that supports developer-friendly defaults, per-endpoint SLAs, cost-control knobs (batching/kv caching), and a clear rollback path. This doc focuses on the delivery contract for hosted customers and handoff items for Dedicated/Private as needed.",
  "requirements": [
    "Unified API surface: single /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings endpoints with explicit type param for chat/completion mode and an opt-in rerank route; backward-compatible aliases maintained for legacy clients.",
    "SDK parity: JS/Python SDKs expose identical method signatures, streaming support for chat & completions, and a high-level rerank helper that accepts candidate lists and returns ranked ids with scores.",
    "Performance targets: P50 token latency < 70ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) on hosted S1 models; P95 < 200ms. Embeddings: P99 < 150ms for 1-4 inputs. Rerank throughput: support 2500 candidate evaluations/sec per allocation.",
    "Reliability: 99.95% availability for hosted endpoints with automatic fallback to smaller model variants when capacity or quota limits are hit.",
    "Cost controls: default server-side batching enabled for multi-request workloads, configurable batching window per API key, and documentation of cost/latency tradeoffs.",
    "Security & privacy: all requests logged with token-level cost metadata; customer data in hosted mode retained for 30 days by default with opt-out. KMS integration required for dedicated/private integrations (see ENG dependency).",
    "Observability: per-route dashboards, request sampling for traces, per-key token cost breakdowns, and regression alerts tied to evaluation prompt sets.",
    "Acceptance test harness: end-to-end test suites in CI that validate correctness for deterministic prompts, streaming order integrity, and rerank stability on seeding datasets.",
    "Rollout controls: canary targeting by API key, region, and plan with automatic rollback on defined SLO regressions."
  ],
  "out_of_scope": [
    "Self-hosted deployment packaging \u2014 Private/Dedicated install artifacts are handled in a separate project; this ticket only defines API contracts for compatibility.",
    "Custom model fine-tuning pipeline \u2014 not part of hosted endpoint initial launch, will be considered post-MVP.",
    "Language-specific SDKs beyond JS/Python for initial launch (Go/Rust scheduled in next cycle)."
  ],
  "scope_changes": [
    "2025-02-20: Removed inline synchronous rerank from /v1/generate path \u2014 introduced dedicated /v1/rerank endpoint to simplify latency SLAs and caching semantics. Decision: improves isolation of compute patterns and enables separate autoscaling.",
    "2025-02-27: Deferred multi-tenant per-request KV-cache pinning to post-launch due to runtime integration complexity (moved to ENG-41820).",
    "2025-03-03: Reduced streaming window default from 250ms to 100ms after QA latency regressions; added explicit SDK opt-in for 'aggressiveStreaming' to avoid surprising cost changes for low-volume users."
  ],
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "API contract: OpenAPI spec published and validated by SDK generation tooling; no breaking changes vs agreed alias mappings.",
    "Performance: Verified in staging with production-like traffic that P50 and P95 latency targets are met for the S1 model family across regions (benchmarks attached).",
    "Stability: End-to-end error rate < 0.5% during a 24-hour stability run with randomized prompt corpus; no data loss on streaming connections longer than 30s.",
    "Security: KMS integration smoke test green and data-retention config enforced for hosted accounts; security review signoff received.",
    "Observability: Dashboards and regression alerts configured; alert playbooks documented and reviewed by on-call rotation.",
    "Docs & SDKs: Public docs (API reference, migration guide, cost guidance) published; JS/Python SDKs have release candidates and integration tests pass.",
    "Rollout: Canary passes defined SLO gates for 72 hours before extending to 50% of traffic; automated rollback works end-to-end."
  ],
  "launch_checklist": [
    "Finalize OpenAPI and example payloads (docs) \u2014 owner: Docs team \u2014 status: todo",
    "SDK release RC1 (JS/Python) with streaming and rerank helpers \u2014 owner: SDK team (ENG-39012) \u2014 status: in progress",
    "Staging perf run and benchmark report \u2014 owner: Performance eng \u2014 status: in progress",
    "Security review & KMS test \u2014 owner: Security \u2014 status: todo",
    "Billing integration for token accounting and plan enforcement \u2014 owner: Billing eng \u2014 status: todo",
    "Canary config created (per-key targeting) and automation jobs defined \u2014 owner: Infra \u2014 status: todo",
    "E2E CI suite passes with randomized prompt sets including rerank fidelity checks \u2014 owner: QA \u2014 status: todo",
    "Create rollback playbook and automate fallback to compact-model variant \u2014 owner: SRE \u2014 status: todo",
    "Customer comms draft (changelog + migration guidance) \u2014 owner: Growth/PM \u2014 status: todo",
    "Post-launch monitoring dashboard and 24/72h escalations staffing plan \u2014 owner: Observability \u2014 status: todo"
  ],
  "rollout_plan": "Week 0: internal dogfooding and integration tests. Week 1: 1% canary (internal + selected customers) for 72h with automated SLO monitoring. Week 2: extend to 25% if canary healthy, monitor cost signals; enable additional regions. Week 3: broad rollout to GA if acceptance gates hold. At every step, feature flags allow disabling streaming or rerank. Rollback path documented to redirect traffic to legacy endpoint aliases and smaller model family.",
  "qa_notes": [
    "Create deterministic seed corpus (1k prompts) that includes streaming edge cases and long-running completions.",
    "Include fuzzing for rerank inputs (duplicate IDs, empty candidate lists, malformed scores).",
    "Validate SDK streaming order using sequence IDs and simulate flaky network conditions.",
    "Run cost smoke tests to ensure batching does not cause token overcount regressions."
  ],
  "review_comments": [
    "Marcus Lee (ENG): 'Agree with splitting rerank to dedicated route \u2014 simplifies autoscaler and lowers tail-latency risk.' \u2014 2025-02-20",
    "Sofia Nguyen (Design): 'Docs need quick-start examples that show cost tradeoffs \u2014 add a 3-step migration snippet.' \u2014 2025-02-22",
    "Priya Desai (Security): 'KMS integration needs an explicit end-to-end test in CI; flagging as required for release.' \u2014 2025-02-25",
    "Ben Carter (PM): 'We should gate GA on billing integration; otherwise customers will hit unexpected charges.' \u2014 2025-03-01"
  ],
  "links": [
    "https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PI/API+Family+Spec+2025",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/412",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/988",
    "https://dashboard.redwood.ai/d/hosted-api/perf-benchmarks?orgId=1",
    "https://docs.redwood.ai/reference/migration-guides/api-family-2025"
  ],

# Hosted API launch readiness

Owner: Ethan Park, Platform & Console
Decision status: Evidence review in progress (product, delivery, and design pass)

## Proposed capability and launch shape

Launch a staged public Hosted API surface for chat, completions, embeddings (single and batches up to 8), and server-side rerank. The contract is REST/OpenAPI, versioned and backward-compatible; core JS/Python SDKs, API-key/OAuth2 authentication, tier-aware quotas, retry guidance, structured chat output, streaming/SSE, deterministic embeddings, and stable rerank semantics are in scope. Dedicated/private deployment bundles and full non-core SDK parity are out of scope. Promotion is staged from internal burn-in to canary, regional expansion, and GA rather than a single all-at-once release. [PM-80421; dsid_6f6a548d740249f6a1413a8ab778f270; /knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/PM-80421-hosted-api-capability-prioritization-acceptance-rollout.json]

## Product gates satisfied by current evidence

- Scope, non-goals, endpoint behavior, versioning, telemetry, SLO targets, rollout stages, and quantitative canary stop conditions are defined in the PRD.
- Design review of Console flows occurred; Leo Martinez requested explicit streaming-interruption error states. This is evidence of review, not final closure of that requested state.
- The delivery specification records agreement to keep rerank on a dedicated route, reducing autoscaler and tail-latency risk.

[PM-80421; dsid_6f6a548d740249f6a1413a8ab778f270; /knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/PM-80421-hosted-api-capability-prioritization-acceptance-rollout.json] [PM-51555; dsid_ada92facaa334d3688c6a8371e0d001a; /knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/PM-51555-api-family-delivery-specification-chat-embeddings-rerank-launch-rundown.json]

## Unresolved delivery items and owners

| Item | Owner | Evidence status |
|---|---|---|
| Final OpenAPI and example payloads | Docs | Todo |
| JS/Python SDK RC1 with streaming/rerank helpers | SDK team / ENG-39012 | In progress |
| Staging performance run and benchmark report | Performance Engineering | In progress |
| Security review and end-to-end KMS test | Security | Todo; required for release |
| Billing token accounting and plan enforcement | Billing Engineering | Todo; PM explicitly gates GA on it |
| Per-key canary config and automation | Infrastructure | Todo |
| Randomized E2E CI including rerank fidelity | QA | Todo |
| Rollback playbook and automated compact-model fallback | SRE | Todo |
| Customer changelog and migration guidance | Growth / PM | Todo |
| Post-launch dashboard and 24/72-hour escalation staffing | Observability | Todo |
| Explicit streaming-interruption error states | Design / Console | Requested; closure not evidenced |
| Streaming verb, default batching window, and embeddings maximum batch choice | PM / API / Runtime | Open decisions in PRD |

Delivery status and owners: [PM-51555; dsid_ada92facaa334d3688c6a8371e0d001a; /knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/PM-51555-api-family-delivery-specification-chat-embeddings-rerank-launch-rundown.json]. Design and PRD open decisions: [PM-80421; dsid_6f6a548d740249f6a1413a8ab778f270; /knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/PM-80421-hosted-api-capability-prioritization-acceptance-rollout.json].

## Current assessment

The capability is product-defined but not launch-ready. This revision deliberately defers a launch recommendation until SRE, security, release, rollback, customer, support, and cohort evidence is reconciled.

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_4a94c098221d4588837f9949309656bc",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/multi-region-availability-slo-2026.json",
    "title": "Multi-Region Availability SLO (2026) — Hosted API + Dedicated",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Multi-Region Availability SLO (2026) \\u2014 Hosted API + Dedicated\",\n  \"space\": \"eng-sre\",\n  \"author\": \"Aisha Bello\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-12-18\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-02-10\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Sean Gallagher\",\n    \"Allison Grant\",\n    \"Miles Thornton\",\n    \"Mina Haddad\",\n    \"Paula Mendes\",\n    \"Tom\\u00e1\\u0161 Nov\\u00e1k\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"slo\",\n    \"error-budget\",\n    \"multi-region\",\n    \"failover\",\n    \"hosted-api\",\n    \"dedicated\",\n    \"reliability-program\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"confluence://eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/regional-failover-automation-upgrade-overview\",\n    \"confluence://architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-042-failover-trigger-signal-hierarchy\",\n    \"confluence://architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-043-automated-routing-policy-rollback\",\n    \"confluence://eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/failover-signal-dashboards-spec\",\n    \"confluence://eng-platform/systems-and-services/region-health-service\"\n  ],\n  \"content\": \"## Purpose\\nThis page defines Redwood Inference\\u2019s **multi-region availability SLOs** for 2026, covering:\\n- **Hosted API** (shared, multi-tenant)\\n- **Dedicated** (reserved capacity, tenant-isolated)\\n\\nThe intent is to:\\n- Measure customer-perceived availability when traffic is eligible for **regional failover**.\\n- Provide clear criteria to distinguish **region-level impairment** (automation-relevant) from partial/localized degradation.\\n- Establish consistent **error budget policies** (alerting, operational response, change management).\\n\\nThis SLO is an internal engineering target and is not a replacement for customer contract language.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## In scope\\n### Products / request paths\\n**Hosted API (paid tiers):**\\n- /v1/chat.completions (streaming + non-streaming)\\n- /v1/completions\\n- /v1/embeddings\\n- /v1/rerank\\n\\n**Dedicated (multi-region enabled tenants only):**\\n- Dedicated endpoints serving the same route families above, behind Dedicated routing policies.\\n\\n### Region eligibility\\nThis SLO applies only to traffic that is:\\n- Routed via Redwood smart routing with **at least one configured failover region**, and\\n- Not constrained by data residency / policy constraints that prevent routing to the configured secondary.\\n\\nIf a tenant is configured single-region only, it is excluded from the multi-region SLO population (but remains covered by single-region service SLOs).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Definitions\\n### Availability (customer-perceived)\\nA request is considered **available** if the Redwood edge/gateway returns a successful response within the request\\u2019s budget:\\n- **Success:** HTTP 2xx or 3xx (including 304) from the customer perspective.\\n- **Unavailable:** HTTP 5xx, gateway timeouts (e.g., 504), and explicit overload rejections (429/503) *when they prevent the route from being served*.\\n\\nNotes:\\n- **Authentication/authorization failures** (401/403) are excluded from availability calculations.\\n- **Customer-caused invalid requests** (400/404/422) are excluded.\\n- **Rate limiting** (429) is excluded only when it is attributable to customer quota/rate policy; 429/503 generated due to platform overload is included.\\n\\n### Multi-region event\\nA **multi-region event** is any incident where customers eligible for failover experience reduced availability due to a regional impairment or the failover system\\u2019s inability to route around it.\\n\\n### Region-level event vs partial degradation\\nWe classify an issue as a **region-level event** when it represents broad impairment of a region\\u2019s ability to serve eligible traffic and is a candidate for automated failover.\\n\\nWe classify as **partial degradation** when the issue is localized (single service, single model family, subset of tenants, or capacity-only without elevated errors) and is typically mitigated by targeted remediation rather than cross-region failover.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## SLO targets (2026)\\n### Summary table\\n| Surface | Population | SLO (availability) | Measurement window |\\n|---|---|---:|---|\\n| Hosted API multi-region | Paid tiers, MR-eligible routes | 99.95% | Rolling 30 days |\\n| Dedicated multi-region | MR-enabled Dedicated tenants/routes | 99.90% | Rolling 30 days |\\n\\nRationale:\\n- Hosted API is expected to sustain higher aggregate availability due to broader regional redundancy and standardized routing.\\n- Dedicated multi-region typically has fewer configured regions and stricter per-tenant constraints; target is set accordingly.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## SLI specification\\n### Hosted API SLI\\n**Indicator:** Request success rate at the **API gateway edge** for MR-eligible traffic.\\n\\n**Good events:**\\n- Count of requests with status_class in {2xx,3xx}\\n\\n**Bad events:**\\n- Count of requests with status_class in {5xx} plus overload responses attributable to platform (429/503 tagged as overload)\\n\\n**Excluded events:**\\n- 401/403\\n- 4xx invalid request classes (400/404/422)\\n- 429 due to tenant quota/rate policy (non-overload)\\n\\n**Segmentation (reporting slices; not all are alerting dimensions):**\\n- route_family: chat.completions | completions | embeddings | rerank\\n- tier: paid (default), enterprise (subset)\\n- traffic_class: interactive | batch (where applicable)\\n\\n**Notes on streaming:**\\n- A streaming request is counted as successful if it returns a 2xx and delivers the first token/byte within the configured gateway budget.\\n- Mid-stream disconnects are tracked separately as a quality metric; only disconnects that manifest as a 5xx to the client count as unavailable.\\n\\n### Dedicated SLI\\n**Indicator:** Request success rate at the Dedicated gateway/edge for MR-enabled tenants.\\n\\n**Good events:** 2xx/3xx\\n\\n**Bad events:** 5xx + overload responses attributable to platform\\n\\n**Excluded events:** same as Hosted.\\n\\n**Tenant segmentation policy:**\\n- SLO measurement is computed at the fleet level for MR-enabled Dedicated traffic.\\n- Per-tenant reporting is available via internal dashboards/audit queries but is not used for global burn-rate paging due to cardinality.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Measurement windows and reporting\\n### Primary compliance window\\n- **Rolling 30-day window** for SLO compliance tracking (Hosted and Dedicated).\\n\\n### Secondary operational windows\\nUsed for detection and burn-rate alerting:\\n- 5m, 30m, 2h, 6h windows (fast burn)\\n- 1d and 7d windows (slow burn)\\n\\nWe use multi-window burn-rate alerting to catch both sharp outages and prolonged degradations.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Error budget policy\\n### Error budget math\\nError budget = 1 - SLO target.\\n- Hosted API MR error budget: 0.05% per 30d\\n- Dedicated MR error budget: 0.10% per 30d\\n\\n### Error budget consumption and required actions\\n| Burn (30d budget) | Interpretation | Required actions |\\n|---:|---|---|\\n| < 25% | Healthy | No special actions. Reliability work continues in normal sprint planning. |\\n| 25\\u201350% | Elevated | SRE + owning teams review top contributors (routes/regions). Add/adjust alerts, dashboards, and mitigations. |\\n| 50\\u2013100% | At risk | Reliability escalation: prioritize mitigations in current cycle. Non-critical launches to routing/failover may require SRE review. |\\n| > 100% | Breached | Declare SLO breach internally; incident review required. Change freeze on failover/routing automation except for reliability fixes and approved mitigations. |\\n\\n### Change management when budgets are at risk\\n- If budget burn is >50% for Hosted or Dedicated MR, changes that can materially affect routing/failover behavior require **SRE on-call reviewer signoff**.\\n- If breached (>100%), a temporary **reliability freeze** applies to:\\n  - routing policy engine behavior changes\\n  - failover controller automation changes\\n  - DNS/traffic steering changes\\n  - gateway retry/timeout behavior changes\\n\\nExceptions:\\n- Fix-forward changes that clearly reduce customer impact may proceed with Director SRE (Sean Gallagher) approval.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## What constitutes a region-level event (classification rules)\\nRegion-level events are used for:\\n- automation trigger validation\\n- incident labeling and reporting\\n- executive reliability reporting\\n\\n### Region-level event (candidate for automated failover)\\nA region is considered **impaired** when BOTH are true:\\n1) **Corroborated reachability or control-plane impairment**\\n   - Cross-region probes indicate reachability failure OR\\n   - Control plane cannot program routing for the region OR\\n   - Provider-level networking symptoms strongly indicate regional impairment\\n\\nAND\\n2) **Customer impact signal in that region\\u2019s serving path**\\n   - Elevated 5xx error burn above threshold for MR-eligible routes OR\\n   - Sustained tail latency burn above threshold AND corroborated by additional signal (e.g., rising timeouts, saturation)\\n\\nMinimum duration (to avoid flapping/noise):\\n- Must persist for **\\u2265 2 minutes** after dampening/hold-down rules (see ADR-042).\\n\\n### Partial degradation (not a region-level event)\\nClassify as partial degradation when one or more of the following holds:\\n- Impact is limited to a single model/version (e.g., one embedding model) while other routes remain healthy.\\n- Impact is isolated to a subset of tenants (e.g., one Dedicated tenant) without evidence of broad regional impairment.\\n- Capacity headroom is low but error/timeout signals are not elevated (mitigate with autoscaling/queueing rather than failover).\\n- A single internal dependency is degraded (e.g., metrics pipeline), but serving remains healthy.\\n\\n### Event severity mapping (operational)\\n| Classification | Typical response | Paging |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| Region-level impairment | Consider/execute regional failover per runbook; enable controller if safe | Page SRE on-call (high urgency) |\\n| Partial degradation | Targeted mitigation; may reduce capacity, roll back model, or adjust autoscaling | Page owning team; SRE if customer-facing and sustained |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Alerting policy (burn-rate)\\nBurn-rate alerts are defined to detect rapid SLO consumption.\\n\\n### Hosted MR availability burn alerts\\n- **Fast burn:** 2h window at 14x budget AND 30m at 14x budget (page)\\n- **Medium burn:** 6h at 6x budget AND 2h at 6x budget (page)\\n- **Slow burn:** 1d at 3x budget AND 6h at 3x budget (ticket + review)\\n\\n### Dedicated MR availability burn alerts\\n- **Fast burn:** 2h at 10x AND 30m at 10x (page)\\n- **Slow burn:** 1d at 2x AND 6h at 2x (ticket + review)\\n\\nAlert annotations must include:\\n- affected route_family\\n- top region(s) by error contribution\\n- current failover state (policy flip status)\\n- links to region health dashboard + incident-bot timeline\\n\\n(See: confluence://eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/failover-signal-dashboards-spec)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Planned events, tests, and exclusions\\n### General rule\\nWe do **not** exclude planned events by default. If customers see errors, it counts.\\n\\n### Controlled failover tests (\\u201cgame days\\u201d)\\nFor production tests:\\n- Tests must be designed to keep customer-visible impact within SLO expectations.\\n- We **tag and report** impact separately (for learning), but it still counts toward the SLO.\\n\\nFor staging and canary-only tests:\\n- Not included in production SLO measurement.\\n\\nDedicated exception (opt-in tests):\\n- If a Dedicated customer explicitly opts into a planned failover test window and acknowledges expected behavior, the window may be excluded from *internal Dedicated MR SLO reporting* for that customer\\u2019s slice, but the global fleet metric remains unchanged.\\n- All exclusions require a change record and must be documented in the game day plan.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Data sources and example queries\\nPrimary data source: gateway request metrics emitted by the edge and aggregated in the SLO toolkit.\\n\\n### Hosted MR availability (conceptual query)\\nAvailability = good / (good + bad)\\n- good: sum(rate(api_gateway_requests_total{population=\\\"mr_eligible\\\", outcome=\\\"good\\\"}[5m]))\\n- bad:  sum(rate(api_gateway_requests_total{population=\\\"mr_eligible\\\", outcome=\\\"bad\\\"}[5m]))\\n\\n### Dedicated MR availability (conceptual query)\\n- good: sum(rate(dedicated_gateway_requests_total{population=\\\"mr_enabled\\\", outcome=\\\"good\\\"}[5m]))\\n- bad:  sum(rate(dedicated_gateway_requests_total{population=\\\"mr_enabled\\\", outcome=\\\"bad\\\"}[5m]))\\n\\nLabeling guidance (cardinality constraints):\\n- Allowed: route_family, tier, region_group, failover_state\\n- Avoid in global SLO metrics: tenant_id, model_id, deployment_id\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Operational expectations and ownership\\n### Owners\\n- SLO definition and reporting: **Eng SRE** (owner: Aisha Bello)\\n- Burn-rate alert rules and dashboards: **Observability** (Allison Grant / Sergio Costa)\\n- Routing + failover behavior: **Smart Routing** (Mina Haddad / Ravi Menon)\\n- Region health aggregation: **Platform** (Ethan Park)\\n\\n### Runbook linkage\\nWhen a Hosted or Dedicated MR burn alert fires, follow:\\n- Hosted: confluence://eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook\\n- Controller operations: confluence://eng-platform/runbooks/routing-policy-failover-controller-runbook\\n- Dedicated drain/evacuation: confluence://eng-infra/runbooks/gpu-pool-drain-and-evacuation-procedure\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Review cadence\\n- Quarterly review of targets and measurement logic.\\n- Post-incident review after any region-level event that consumes >10% of monthly error budget.\\n- Annual update each December for the next year\\u2019s SLO plan.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Change log\\n- 2025-12-18: Initial 2026 definition drafted (Hosted + Dedicated MR populations).\\n- 2026-01-06: Clarified streaming success criteria and overload inclusion.\\n- 2026-01-22: Added Dedicated opt-in planned test exclusion guidance; tightened classification rules.\\n- 2026-02-10: Updated burn-rate alert multipliers to match current paging hygiene guidance; added labeling/cardinality constraints.\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": {
  "title": "Multi-Region Availability SLO (2026) — Hosted API + Dedicated",
  "space": "eng-sre",
  "author": "Aisha Bello",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2025-12-18",
  "last_updated": "2026-02-10",
  "reviewers": [
    "Sean Gallagher",
    "Allison Grant",
    "Miles Thornton",
    "Mina Haddad",
    "Paula Mendes",
    "Tomáš Novák"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "slo",
    "error-budget",
    "multi-region",
    "failover",
    "hosted-api",
    "dedicated",
    "reliability-program"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "related_pages": [
    "confluence://eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/regional-failover-automation-upgrade-overview",
    "confluence://architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-042-failover-trigger-signal-hierarchy",
    "confluence://architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-043-automated-routing-policy-rollback",
    "confluence://eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/failover-signal-dashboards-spec",
    "confluence://eng-platform/systems-and-services/region-health-service"
  ],
  "content": "## Purpose
This page defines Redwood Inference’s **multi-region availability SLOs** for 2026, covering:
- **Hosted API** (shared, multi-tenant)
- **Dedicated** (reserved capacity, tenant-isolated)

The intent is to:
- Measure customer-perceived availability when traffic is eligible for **regional failover**.
- Provide clear criteria to distinguish **region-level impairment** (automation-relevant) from partial/localized degradation.
- Establish consistent **error budget policies** (alerting, operational response, change management).

This SLO is an internal engineering target and is not a replacement for customer contract language.

---

## In scope
### Products / request paths
**Hosted API (paid tiers):**
- /v1/chat.completions (streaming + non-streaming)
- /v1/completions
- /v1/embeddings
- /v1/rerank

**Dedicated (multi-region enabled tenants only):**
- Dedicated endpoints serving the same route families above, behind Dedicated routing policies.

### Region eligibility
This SLO applies only to traffic that is:
- Routed via Redwood smart routing with **at least one configured failover region**, and
- Not constrained by data residency / policy constraints that prevent routing to the configured secondary.

If a tenant is configured single-region only, it is excluded from the multi-region SLO population (but remains covered by single-region service SLOs).

---

## Definitions
### Availability (customer-perceived)
A request is considered **available** if the Redwood edge/gateway returns a successful response within the request’s budget:
- **Success:** HTTP 2xx or 3xx (including 304) from the customer perspective.
- **Unavailable:** HTTP 5xx, gateway timeouts (e.g., 504), and explicit overload rejections (429/503) *when they prevent the route from being served*.

Notes:
- **Authentication/authorization failures** (401/403) are excluded from availability calculations.
- **Customer-caused invalid requests** (400/404/422) are excluded.
- **Rate limiting** (429) is excluded only when it is attributable to customer quota/rate policy; 429/503 generated due to platform overload is included.

### Multi-region event
A **multi-region event** is any incident where customers eligible for failover experience reduced availability due to a regional impairment or the failover system’s inability to route around it.

### Region-level event vs partial degradation
We classify an issue as a **region-level event** when it represents broad impairment of a region’s ability to serve eligible traffic and is a candidate for automated failover.

We classify as **partial degradation** when the issue is localized (single service, single model family, subset of tenants, or capacity-only without elevated errors) and is typically mitigated by targeted remediation rather than cross-region failover.

---

## SLO targets (2026)
### Summary table
| Surface | Population | SLO (availability) | Measurement window |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Hosted API multi-region | Paid tiers, MR-eligible routes | 99.95% | Rolling 30 days |
| Dedicated multi-region | MR-enabled Dedicated tenants/routes | 99.90% | Rolling 30 days |

Rationale:
- Hosted API is expected to sustain higher aggregate availability due to broader regional redundancy and standardized routing.
- Dedicated multi-region typically has fewer configured regions and stricter per-tenant constraints; target is set accordingly.

---

## SLI specification
### Hosted API SLI
**Indicator:** Request success rate at the **API gateway edge** for MR-eligible traffic.

**Good events:**
- Count of requests with status_class in {2xx,3xx}

**Bad events:**
- Count of requests with status_class in {5xx} plus overload responses attributable to platform (429/503 tagged as overload)

**Excluded events:**
- 401/403
- 4xx invalid request classes (400/404/422)
- 429 due to tenant quota/rate policy (non-overload)

**Segmentation (reporting slices; not all are alerting dimensions):**
- route_family: chat.completions | completions | embeddings | rerank
- tier: paid (default), enterprise (subset)
- traffic_class: interactive | batch (where applicable)

**Notes on streaming:**
- A streaming request is counted as successful if it returns a 2xx and delivers the first token/byte within the configured gateway budget.
- Mid-stream disconnects are tracked separately as a quality metric; only disconnects that manifest as a 5xx to the client count as unavailable.

### Dedicated SLI
**Indicator:** Request success rate at the Dedicated gateway/edge for MR-enabled tenants.

**Good events:** 2xx/3xx

**Bad events:** 5xx + overload responses attributable to platform

**Excluded events:** same as Hosted.

**Tenant segmentation policy:**
- SLO measurement is computed at the fleet level for MR-enabled Dedicated traffic.
- Per-tenant reporting is available via internal dashboards/audit queries but is not used for global burn-rate paging due to cardinality.

---

## Measurement windows and reporting
### Primary compliance window
- **Rolling 30-day window** for SLO compliance tracking (Hosted and Dedicated).

### Secondary operational windows
Used for detection and burn-rate alerting:
- 5m, 30m, 2h, 6h windows (fast burn)
- 1d and 7d windows (slow burn)

We use multi-window burn-rate alerting to catch both sharp outages and prolonged degradations.

---

## Error budget policy
### Error budget math
Error budget = 1 - SLO target.
- Hosted API MR error budget: 0.05% per 30d
- Dedicated MR error budget: 0.10% per 30d

### Error budget consumption and required actions
| Burn (30d budget) | Interpretation | Required actions |
|---:|---|---|
| < 25% | Healthy | No special actions. Reliability work continues in normal sprint planning. |
| 25–50% | Elevated | SRE + owning teams review top contributors (routes/regions). Add/adjust alerts, dashboards, and mitigations. |
| 50–100% | At risk | Reliability escalation: prioritize mitigations in current cycle. Non-critical launches to routing/failover may require SRE review. |
| > 100% | Breached | Declare SLO breach internally; incident review required. Change freeze on failover/routing automation except for reliability fixes and approved mitigations. |

### Change management when budgets are at risk
- If budget burn is >50% for Hosted or Dedicated MR, changes that can materially affect routing/failover behavior require **SRE on-call reviewer signoff**.
- If breached (>100%), a temporary **reliability freeze** applies to:
  - routing policy engine behavior changes
  - failover controller automation changes
  - DNS/traffic steering changes
  - gateway retry/timeout behavior changes

Exceptions:
- Fix-forward changes that clearly reduce customer impact may proceed with Director SRE (Sean Gallagher) approval.

---

## What constitutes a region-level event (classification rules)
Region-level events are used for:
- automation trigger validation
- incident labeling and reporting
- executive reliability reporting

### Region-level event (candidate for automated failover)
A region is considered **impaired** when BOTH are true:
1) **Corroborated reachability or control-plane impairment**
   - Cross-region probes indicate reachability failure OR
   - Control plane cannot program routing for the region OR
   - Provider-level networking symptoms strongly indicate regional impairment

AND
2) **Customer impact signal in that region’s serving path**
   - Elevated 5xx error burn above threshold for MR-eligible routes OR
   - Sustained tail latency burn above threshold AND corroborated by additional signal (e.g., rising timeouts, saturation)

Minimum duration (to avoid flapping/noise):
- Must persist for **≥ 2 minutes** after dampening/hold-down rules (see ADR-042).

### Partial degradation (not a region-level event)
Classify as partial degradation when one or more of the following holds:
- Impact is limited to a single model/version (e.g., one embedding model) while other routes remain healthy.
- Impact is isolated to a subset of tenants (e.g., one Dedicated tenant) without evidence of broad regional impairment.
- Capacity headroom is low but error/timeout signals are not elevated (mitigate with autoscaling/queueing rather than failover).
- A single internal dependency is degraded (e.g., metrics pipeline), but serving remains healthy.

### Event severity mapping (operational)
| Classification | Typical response | Paging |
|---|---|---|
| Region-level impairment | Consider/execute regional failover per runbook; enable controller if safe | Page SRE on-call (high urgency) |
| Partial degradation | Targeted mitigation; may reduce capacity, roll back model, or adjust autoscaling | Page owning team; SRE if customer-facing and sustained |

---

## Alerting policy (burn-rate)
Burn-rate alerts are defined to detect rapid SLO consumption.

### Hosted MR availability burn alerts
- **Fast burn:** 2h window at 14x budget AND 30m at 14x budget (page)
- **Medium burn:** 6h at 6x budget AND 2h at 6x budget (page)
- **Slow burn:** 1d at 3x budget AND 6h at 3x budget (ticket + review)

### Dedicated MR availability burn alerts
- **Fast burn:** 2h at 10x AND 30m at 10x (page)
- **Slow burn:** 1d at 2x AND 6h at 2x (ticket + review)

Alert annotations must include:
- affected route_family
- top region(s) by error contribution
- current failover state (policy flip status)
- links to region health dashboard + incident-bot timeline

(See: confluence://eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/failover-signal-dashboards-spec)

---

## Planned events, tests, and exclusions
### General rule
We do **not** exclude planned events by default. If customers see errors, it counts.

### Controlled failover tests (“game days”)
For production tests:
- Tests must be designed to keep customer-visible impact within SLO expectations.
- We **tag and report** impact separately (for learning), but it still counts toward the SLO.

For staging and canary-only tests:
- Not included in production SLO measurement.

Dedicated exception (opt-in tests):
- If a Dedicated customer explicitly opts into a planned failover test window and acknowledges expected behavior, the window may be excluded from *internal Dedicated MR SLO reporting* for that customer’s slice, but the global fleet metric remains unchanged.
- All exclusions require a change record and must be documented in the game day plan.

---

## Data sources and example queries
Primary data source: gateway request metrics emitted by the edge and aggregated in the SLO toolkit.

### Hosted MR availability (conceptual query)
Availability = good / (good + bad)
- good: sum(rate(api_gateway_requests_total{population="mr_eligible", outcome="good"}[5m]))
- bad:  sum(rate(api_gateway_requests_total{population="mr_eligible", outcome="bad"}[5m]))

### Dedicated MR availability (conceptual query)
- good: sum(rate(dedicated_gateway_requests_total{population="mr_enabled", outcome="good"}[5m]))
- bad:  sum(rate(dedicated_gateway_requests_total{population="mr_enabled", outcome="bad"}[5m]))

Labeling guidance (cardinality constraints):
- Allowed: route_family, tier, region_group, failover_state
- Avoid in global SLO metrics: tenant_id, model_id, deployment_id

---

## Operational expectations and ownership
### Owners
- SLO definition and reporting: **Eng SRE** (owner: Aisha Bello)
- Burn-rate alert rules and dashboards: **Observability** (Allison Grant / Sergio Costa)
- Routing + failover behavior: **Smart Routing** (Mina Haddad / Ravi Menon)
- Region health aggregation: **Platform** (Ethan Park)

### Runbook linkage
When a Hosted or Dedicated MR burn alert fires, follow:
- Hosted: confluence://eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook
- Controller operations: confluence://eng-platform/runbooks/routing-policy-failover-controller-runbook
- Dedicated drain/evacuation: confluence://eng-infra/runbooks/gpu-pool-drain-and-evacuation-procedure

---

## Review cadence
- Quarterly review of targets and measurement logic.
- Post-incident review after any region-level event that consumes >10% of monthly error budget.
- Annual update each December for the next year’s SLO plan.

---

## Change log
- 2025-12-18: Initial 2026 definition drafted (Hosted + Dedicated MR populations).
- 2026-01-06: Clarified streaming success criteria and overload inclusion.
- 2026-01-22: Added Dedicated opt-in planned test exclusion guidance; tightened classification rules.
- 2026-02-10: Updated burn-rate alert multipliers to match current paging hygiene guidance; added labeling/cardinality constraints.

  "body": "Owner: Connor O\u2019Brien (Release)\nLast reviewed: 2025-04-04\nScope: GA enablement for \u201cHosted canary rollout workflow\u201d (percentage-based traffic splitting on Hosted routes) including Console UI, control plane schema, policy guardrails, routing enforcement, telemetry + dashboards, audit logging.\n\nThis checklist is written for the GA cut + staged enablement (beta \u2192 GA) and should be used as the \u201csingle source of truth\u201d for release go/no-go readiness and backout steps.\n\n---\n\n1) Release metadata\n\nRelease name: Hosted Canary Rollouts \u2014 GA\nTarget window: Week of 2025-04-07 (Mon\u2013Thu)\nPrimary on-call coverage required: Eng Platform + SRE\nChange classification: Customer-facing feature w/ routing dataplane behavior + new policy paths + audit logging\nBlast radius: Per-tenant by feature flag; dataplane change affects routing decisions only when rollout config exists OR flag gates are enabled.\n\nApprovers (required for GA flip):\n- Product: Marissa Cole (Console & rollouts) + Paula Mendes (policy/telemetry requirements)\n- Engineering: Dylan Brooks (Console & tooling), Ethan Park (Control Plane), Mina Haddad (Smart Routing)\n- SRE: Sean Gallagher (SRE lead) or Rafael Mendes (on-call manager)\n- Security: Marcus Lin (audit logging/RBAC)\n- Release: Connor O\u2019Brien\n\nGo/no-go meeting: 30 mins, day-of enablement\nAgenda: open Sev bugs, SLO/alert readiness, runbook readiness, kill switch confirmation, audit log verification, staged rollout plan\n\n---\n\n2) Dependencies (must be merged + deployed prior to GA)\n\nCode deployed to production (verify commit SHAs / deploy IDs in deploy tool):\n[ ] Smart Routing traffic splitting primitive deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28741)\n[ ] Rollout Orchestrator API + state machine deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28788)\n[ ] Policy engine guardrails deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28802)\n[ ] Telemetry tagging + aggregation hooks deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28819)\n[ ] Auto-stop / rollback wiring deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28845)\n[ ] Activity timeline + audit events persistence deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28877)\n[ ] Cohort dashboards/alert templates available (GitHub: redwood/pr-28910)\n\nRBAC + permissions:\n[ ] rollout-approver role + permission mappings deployed (GitHub: rbac-policy-bundle/pr-311)\n[ ] Console correctly hides/disables actions when perms missing (create/start/approve/pause/rollback)\n\nDocs readiness:\n[ ] Customer docs merged + published (GitHub: redwood-docs/pr-922)\n[ ] Internal on-call runbook final (Confluence: runbook-rollout-stuck-or-bad-split)\n[ ] Audit event spec final + shared w/ Support/Sales (Confluence: audit-events-rollout-actions)\n\n---\n\n3) Feature flags / config gates\n\nWe are using a layered gating approach. GA requires all three layers to be \u201cready,\u201d but only tenant-level enablement should be expanded.\n\nA) Console UI gating\nFlag: console.hosted_canary_rollouts_ui\nDefault: OFF\nControls: visibility of Rollouts wizard + timeline views in Console\nChecklist:\n[ ] Flag exists in prod, is writable by release tooling\n[ ] Flag OFF behavior is clean (no dead links, no partial panels)\n[ ] Flag ON for internal dogfood tenants only pre-GA\n\nB) Control plane / orchestrator gating\nFlag: control_plane.hosted_canary_rollouts_orchestrator\nDefault: ON (recommended) or ON for allowlist only depending on risk call\nControls: create/progress/pause/rollback endpoints acceptance; persistence paths\nChecklist:\n[ ] Validate no background tasks run for tenants without rollouts configured\n[ ] Validate idempotency on action endpoints (retry safe)\n[ ] Verify orchestrator emits events even when Console UI is off (API-only tenants)\n\nC) Dataplane enforcement gating\nFlag: routing.hosted_route_canary_splitting\nDefault: ON (recommended) but only used when a rollout is active OR allowlist\nControls: actual traffic splitting enforcement for Hosted routes\nChecklist:\n[ ] Verify enforcement is no-op unless rollout config present / active\n[ ] Verify deterministic cohorting key per ADR (Confluence ADR: cohorting & traffic splitting)\n[ ] Verify region behavior matches GA spec (percent is global per route; region-specific metrics available)\n\nKill switches (must exist + verified):\n[ ] Kill switch 1: disable routing enforcement (routing.hosted_route_canary_splitting = OFF)\n[ ] Kill switch 2: block new rollouts creation/start for new tenants (control_plane\u2026 allowlist mode)\n[ ] Kill switch 3: hide Console entry points (console\u2026 = OFF)\n\nKill switch ownership + execution:\nPrimary: SRE on-call (Sean/Rafael) can flip routing kill switch\nSecondary: Release (Connor) can flip Console flag\nTertiary: Control plane on-call (Ethan\u2019s rotation) can switch orchestrator allowlist mode\n\n---\n\n4) Migrations / schema changes\n\nSchema changes (control plane persistence): rollout objects, steps/states, audit/event references (ENG-9131)\n\nPre-flight:\n[ ] Confirm migrations are backward compatible with existing routing policy schema\n[ ] Confirm read paths tolerate missing new fields (safe defaults)\n[ ] Confirm old Console clients do not crash if new rollout data exists\n\nExecution:\n[ ] Migration applied to prod control-plane DB(s) during low-traffic window\n[ ] Verify migration completion: no long locks, no replication lag above threshold\n[ ] Verify new tables/columns have correct indexes (rollout_id lookups, route_id lookups)\n\nPost-migration validation:\n[ ] Create a test rollout in staging and prod-internal tenant; confirm persists and reads back\n[ ] Confirm audit event persistence works (rollout_create, rollout_start, step_change, pause, approval, rollback)\n[ ] Confirm event retention settings align with security expectations (per audit logging spec)\n\nRollback stance for migrations:\n- Prefer forward-fix: schema additions are not rolled back unless necessary (risk of data loss).\n- If hard rollback required: stop all orchestrator writes + disable UI + disable routing enforcement first, then consult DB owner for recovery.\n\n---\n\n5) Monitoring, dashboards, and alerting to watch\n\nKey signals for release window (must be pinned in the \u201cGA watch\u201d dashboard):\n\nA) Routing correctness\n[ ] Split adherence: observed canary % vs configured % (global + per-region)\n[ ] Cohort assignment stability: % of requests switching cohorts for same user key (should be ~0; watch streaming/retries)\n[ ] Retry behavior: ensure retries do not flip cohort unexpectedly\n\nB) Customer-impact SLO signals (baseline vs canary)\n[ ] 5xx rate (baseline cohort vs canary cohort)\n[ ] timeout rate (baseline vs canary)\n[ ] p95 latency (baseline vs canary)\n[ ] queue time / admission control signals (if applicable)\n\nC) System health\n[ ] Control plane API error rate on rollout endpoints\n[ ] Orchestrator background worker lag / stuck transitions\n[ ] Metric evaluation timeouts for stop conditions (watch for repeat of beta issue fixed in pr-28895)\n[ ] Audit log pipeline: ingestion success rate and export queue depth (if enabled)\n\nAlert policy during GA window (tuning guidance):\n- Avoid alert storms: cohort-specific alerts should page only when BOTH: (a) minimum traffic threshold met AND (b) regression above threshold sustained for N minutes.\n- Ensure stop-condition triggers do not page twice (auto-pause + alert) unless necessary.\n\nConfirm templates exist:\n[ ] Standard cohort comparison panels available (GitHub: observability-pack/pr-184 or redwood/pr-28910)\n[ ] Alert templates for auto-stop triggers reviewed by SRE (Sean/Rafael)\n\n---\n\n6) Auto-stop / auto-rollback configuration\n\nDefault stop conditions (GA defaults) \u2014 confirm they match product decision + SRE sign-off:\n[ ] 5xx regression threshold: ____% absolute or ____x relative (fill in final values)\n[ ] timeout regression threshold: ____% absolute\n[ ] p95 latency regression threshold: +____ ms or +____% over baseline\n[ ] Minimum sample size / minimum time window before evaluating: ____\n[ ] Soak time minimum between steps: ____ (policy enforced)\n\nSafety checks:\n[ ] Confirm auto-stop action is PAUSE by default (vs rollback), unless tenant policy requires rollback\n[ ] Confirm rollback is a separate explicit action or only happens after pause + approval (depending on tier)\n[ ] Confirm notifications route to correct internal channels for beta/GA (PagerDuty + Slack)\n\nRunbook linkage:\n[ ] Stop-condition fired path referenced in runbook (diagnostics, how to resume/rollback)\n\n---\n\n7) Approval gates / policy guardrails verification\n\nGuardrails required for GA (PM-1851):\n[ ] Max step size enforced (e.g., cannot jump from 5% to 100% unless policy allows)\n[ ] Minimum soak time enforced between step promotions\n[ ] Approval required for risky actions (configurable): start rollout, promote above threshold, rollback\n[ ] Clear Console error messages on deny with \u201chow to fix\u201d guidance\n\nRBAC behaviors:\n[ ] Non-approver cannot approve steps / cannot override guardrails\n[ ] Approver role can approve but still cannot exceed hard tenant policy caps\n[ ] Audit events record actor, role, IP/user agent (as available), tenant, route, diffs\n\nEdge cases to test (quick checklist):\n[ ] Attempt to promote before soak time elapsed \u2192 denied, message displayed\n[ ] Attempt step > max jump \u2192 denied\n[ ] Attempt rollback without permission \u2192 denied\n[ ] Attempt start while missing required metrics (no traffic) \u2192 allowed but stop conditions should not thrash\n\n---\n\n8) Release sequencing plan (staged enablement)\n\nStage 0 \u2014 Internal dogfood (already in progress)\n[ ] Enable for Redwood internal tenant(s) only\n[ ] Run 1\u20132 real rollouts of non-critical Hosted routes\n[ ] Validate audit logs show up in internal audit viewer\n\nStage 1 \u2014 Design partner cohort (beta) stability check\n[ ] Confirm no open P0/P1 issues from design partners tracker\n[ ] Confirm support escalation path is active (#support-escalations + on-call)\n\nStage 2 \u2014 GA soft launch (allowlist)\nTarget: 10\u201320 tenants over first 48 hours\n[ ] Enable tenant flag for first batch (coordinate w/ Support + PM)\n[ ] Watch dashboards for 1 hour after each batch\n[ ] Freeze further enablement if any routing correctness anomalies\n\nStage 3 \u2014 GA broad availability\n[ ] Switch default enablement from allowlist \u2192 available-by-request \u2192 self-serve (per product decision)\n[ ] Update support macros and internal enablement how-to\n\n---\n\n9) Backout / incident plan\n\nPrinciple: Prefer \u201cstop the bleeding\u201d (disable enforcement) over partial rollbacks.\n\nBackout levels (execute in this order for highest safety):\n\nLevel 1: Disable routing enforcement (fastest)\n- Action: routing.hosted_route_canary_splitting = OFF\n- Effect: all traffic goes to baseline routing behavior; rollouts remain visible but do not affect split\n- Owner: SRE on-call\n- Verification: canary cohort traffic drops to ~0% within 5\u201310 minutes; error rate normalizes\n\nLevel 2: Pause rollouts globally / block new rollouts\n- Action: control_plane.hosted_canary_rollouts_orchestrator = allowlist-only OR \u201cwrites disabled\u201d mode\n- Effect: prevents new rollouts / step promotions; existing rollouts can be paused (manual)\n- Owner: Control plane on-call\n\nLevel 3: Hide Console UI entry points\n- Action: console.hosted_canary_rollouts_ui = OFF\n- Effect: customers can\u2019t initiate via Console; reduces load on support while investigation proceeds\n- Owner: Release / Console on-call\n\nLevel 4: Full service rollback (last resort)\n- Roll back orchestrator/routing builds only if a safe previous version is known-good and compatible with new schema.\n- Requires: engineering leads approval (Dylan/Ethan/Mina) + SRE approval\n\nIncident triggers (examples):\n- Observed split mismatch > 2x expected sustained for > 15 minutes (e.g., config 10%, observed 30%)\n- Cross-region inconsistency causing higher-than-expected canary traffic in a single region\n- Auto-stop thrashing (pause/resume loops) affecting customer operations\n- Audit logging failure for rollout actions (security regression)\n\nComms plan during incident:\n[ ] Start internal incident channel (if Sev2+)\n[ ] Notify Support lead (Dev Patel) and create/update customer comms snippet\n[ ] For impacted enterprise tenants: direct CSM outreach\n\n---\n\n10) Verification tests (release-day run)\n\nStaging:\n[ ] Run E2E: create \u2192 start \u2192 1% step \u2192 promote \u2192 pause \u2192 rollback \u2192 confirm baseline restored\n[ ] Run E2E with approval required: start denied until approver approves\n[ ] Force stop-condition breach in staging and verify auto-pause + notification\n\nProduction (internal tenant only):\n[ ] Create rollout on a low-risk internal Hosted route\n[ ] Confirm observed traffic split matches within tolerance (after warmup)\n[ ] Confirm dashboards show baseline vs canary metrics with correct tags\n[ ] Confirm audit events emitted and visible (and exportable if configured)\n\nPost-enablement spot checks (first external tenants):\n[ ] Confirm tenant can see rollout wizard + timeline\n[ ] Confirm policy guardrails reflect tenant tier (max step, approvals)\n[ ] Confirm support can retrieve rollout_id, state, and recent actions quickly\n\n---\n\n11) Documentation + support readiness\n\nCustomer docs:\n[ ] \u201cHow to run a canary rollout\u201d updated with screenshots and guardrail explanations\n[ ] Troubleshooting section includes: split mismatch, auto-paused, stuck step, approval denied\n\nInternal docs:\n[ ] How-to enable feature for tenant is accurate and includes sanity checks\n[ ] On-call runbook includes: diagnosing wrong split, disabling enforcement, checking cohort tags\n\nSupport enablement:\n[ ] Support macro for \u201cHow do I do a percentage rollout?\u201d includes current GA availability rules\n[ ] Escalation template includes required fields: tenant_id, route_id, rollout_id, region, timestamps, expected %\n\n---\n\n12) Final sign-offs (fill in during go/no-go)\n\nProduct sign-off:\n- Marissa Cole: ____ (date/time)\n- Paula Mendes: ____ (date/time)\n\nEngineering sign-off:\n- Dylan Brooks: ____ (date/time)\n- Ethan Park: ____ (date/time)\n- Mina Haddad: ____ (date/time)\n\nSRE sign-off:\n- Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes: ____ (date/time)\n\nSecurity sign-off:\n- Marcus Lin: ____ (date/time)\n\nRelease sign-off:\n- Connor O\u2019Brien: ____ (date/time)\n\nNotes / open items at time of GA:\n- \n- \n\nAppendix: Known GA limitations (keep aligned with PM-1859)\n- No multi-armed bandits / dynamic optimization\n- Quality gates are optional/manual inputs only; not a blocking automated gate for GA\n- Dedicated/Private parity not in GA scope; ensure schema compatibility only\n",
