    "Linear:ENG-9171",
    "GitHub:redwood/pr-28741-hosted-route-canary-split-routing-primitive",
    "GitHub:redwood/pr-28788-rollout-orchestrator-api-create-progress-pause-rollback",
    "GitHub:redwood/pr-28802-policy-engine-guardrails-for-rollout-actions",
    "GitHub:redwood/pr-28819-telemetry-tagging-rollout-id-and-cohort",
    "GitHub:redwood/pr-28845-auto-stop-rollback-on-slo-breach",
    "GitHub:redwood/pr-28877-rollout-activity-log-and-audit-events",
    "GitHub:redwood/pr-28910-add-rollout-cohort-dashboards-and-alert-templates",
    "GitHub:redwood-docs/pr-922-console-hosted-canary-rollouts-ga-docs",
    "GitHub:rbac-policy-bundle/pr-311-rollout-approver-role-and-permissions",
    "Confluence:architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-hosted-rollout-cohorting-and-traffic-splitting",
    "Confluence:oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/runbook-rollout-stuck-or-bad-split",
    "Confluence:security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-events-rollout-actions",
    "Slack:eng-releases/1740638401-beta-enablement-schedule-and-kill-switch"
  ],
  "body": "Owner: Connor O’Brien (Release)
Last reviewed: 2025-04-04
Scope: GA enablement for “Hosted canary rollout workflow” (percentage-based traffic splitting on Hosted routes) including Console UI, control plane schema, policy guardrails, routing enforcement, telemetry + dashboards, audit logging.

This checklist is written for the GA cut + staged enablement (beta → GA) and should be used as the “single source of truth” for release go/no-go readiness and backout steps.

---

1) Release metadata

Release name: Hosted Canary Rollouts — GA
Target window: Week of 2025-04-07 (Mon–Thu)
Primary on-call coverage required: Eng Platform + SRE
Change classification: Customer-facing feature w/ routing dataplane behavior + new policy paths + audit logging
Blast radius: Per-tenant by feature flag; dataplane change affects routing decisions only when rollout config exists OR flag gates are enabled.

Approvers (required for GA flip):
- Product: Marissa Cole (Console & rollouts) + Paula Mendes (policy/telemetry requirements)
- Engineering: Dylan Brooks (Console & tooling), Ethan Park (Control Plane), Mina Haddad (Smart Routing)
- SRE: Sean Gallagher (SRE lead) or Rafael Mendes (on-call manager)
- Security: Marcus Lin (audit logging/RBAC)
- Release: Connor O’Brien

Go/no-go meeting: 30 mins, day-of enablement
Agenda: open Sev bugs, SLO/alert readiness, runbook readiness, kill switch confirmation, audit log verification, staged rollout plan

---

2) Dependencies (must be merged + deployed prior to GA)

Code deployed to production (verify commit SHAs / deploy IDs in deploy tool):
[ ] Smart Routing traffic splitting primitive deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28741)
[ ] Rollout Orchestrator API + state machine deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28788)
[ ] Policy engine guardrails deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28802)
[ ] Telemetry tagging + aggregation hooks deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28819)
[ ] Auto-stop / rollback wiring deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28845)
[ ] Activity timeline + audit events persistence deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28877)
[ ] Cohort dashboards/alert templates available (GitHub: redwood/pr-28910)

RBAC + permissions:
[ ] rollout-approver role + permission mappings deployed (GitHub: rbac-policy-bundle/pr-311)
[ ] Console correctly hides/disables actions when perms missing (create/start/approve/pause/rollback)

Docs readiness:
[ ] Customer docs merged + published (GitHub: redwood-docs/pr-922)
[ ] Internal on-call runbook final (Confluence: runbook-rollout-stuck-or-bad-split)
[ ] Audit event spec final + shared w/ Support/Sales (Confluence: audit-events-rollout-actions)

---

3) Feature flags / config gates

We are using a layered gating approach. GA requires all three layers to be “ready,” but only tenant-level enablement should be expanded.

A) Console UI gating
Flag: console.hosted_canary_rollouts_ui
Default: OFF
Controls: visibility of Rollouts wizard + timeline views in Console
Checklist:
[ ] Flag exists in prod, is writable by release tooling
[ ] Flag OFF behavior is clean (no dead links, no partial panels)
[ ] Flag ON for internal dogfood tenants only pre-GA

B) Control plane / orchestrator gating
Flag: control_plane.hosted_canary_rollouts_orchestrator
Default: ON (recommended) or ON for allowlist only depending on risk call
Controls: create/progress/pause/rollback endpoints acceptance; persistence paths
Checklist:
[ ] Validate no background tasks run for tenants without rollouts configured
[ ] Validate idempotency on action endpoints (retry safe)
[ ] Verify orchestrator emits events even when Console UI is off (API-only tenants)

C) Dataplane enforcement gating
Flag: routing.hosted_route_canary_splitting
Default: ON (recommended) but only used when a rollout is active OR allowlist
Controls: actual traffic splitting enforcement for Hosted routes
Checklist:
[ ] Verify enforcement is no-op unless rollout config present / active
[ ] Verify deterministic cohorting key per ADR (Confluence ADR: cohorting & traffic splitting)
[ ] Verify region behavior matches GA spec (percent is global per route; region-specific metrics available)

Kill switches (must exist + verified):
[ ] Kill switch 1: disable routing enforcement (routing.hosted_route_canary_splitting = OFF)
[ ] Kill switch 2: block new rollouts creation/start for new tenants (control_plane… allowlist mode)
[ ] Kill switch 3: hide Console entry points (console… = OFF)

Kill switch ownership + execution:
Primary: SRE on-call (Sean/Rafael) can flip routing kill switch
Secondary: Release (Connor) can flip Console flag
Tertiary: Control plane on-call (Ethan’s rotation) can switch orchestrator allowlist mode

---

4) Migrations / schema changes

Schema changes (control plane persistence): rollout objects, steps/states, audit/event references (ENG-9131)

Pre-flight:
[ ] Confirm migrations are backward compatible with existing routing policy schema
[ ] Confirm read paths tolerate missing new fields (safe defaults)
[ ] Confirm old Console clients do not crash if new rollout data exists

Execution:
[ ] Migration applied to prod control-plane DB(s) during low-traffic window
[ ] Verify migration completion: no long locks, no replication lag above threshold
[ ] Verify new tables/columns have correct indexes (rollout_id lookups, route_id lookups)

Post-migration validation:
[ ] Create a test rollout in staging and prod-internal tenant; confirm persists and reads back
[ ] Confirm audit event persistence works (rollout_create, rollout_start, step_change, pause, approval, rollback)
[ ] Confirm event retention settings align with security expectations (per audit logging spec)

Rollback stance for migrations:
- Prefer forward-fix: schema additions are not rolled back unless necessary (risk of data loss).
- If hard rollback required: stop all orchestrator writes + disable UI + disable routing enforcement first, then consult DB owner for recovery.

---

5) Monitoring, dashboards, and alerting to watch

Key signals for release window (must be pinned in the “GA watch” dashboard):

A) Routing correctness
[ ] Split adherence: observed canary % vs configured % (global + per-region)
[ ] Cohort assignment stability: % of requests switching cohorts for same user key (should be ~0; watch streaming/retries)
[ ] Retry behavior: ensure retries do not flip cohort unexpectedly

B) Customer-impact SLO signals (baseline vs canary)
[ ] 5xx rate (baseline cohort vs canary cohort)
[ ] timeout rate (baseline vs canary)
[ ] p95 latency (baseline vs canary)
[ ] queue time / admission control signals (if applicable)

C) System health
[ ] Control plane API error rate on rollout endpoints
[ ] Orchestrator background worker lag / stuck transitions
[ ] Metric evaluation timeouts for stop conditions (watch for repeat of beta issue fixed in pr-28895)
[ ] Audit log pipeline: ingestion success rate and export queue depth (if enabled)

Alert policy during GA window (tuning guidance):
- Avoid alert storms: cohort-specific alerts should page only when BOTH: (a) minimum traffic threshold met AND (b) regression above threshold sustained for N minutes.
- Ensure stop-condition triggers do not page twice (auto-pause + alert) unless necessary.

Confirm templates exist:
[ ] Standard cohort comparison panels available (GitHub: observability-pack/pr-184 or redwood/pr-28910)
[ ] Alert templates for auto-stop triggers reviewed by SRE (Sean/Rafael)

---

6) Auto-stop / auto-rollback configuration

Default stop conditions (GA defaults) — confirm they match product decision + SRE sign-off:
[ ] 5xx regression threshold: ____% absolute or ____x relative (fill in final values)
[ ] timeout regression threshold: ____% absolute
[ ] p95 latency regression threshold: +____ ms or +____% over baseline
[ ] Minimum sample size / minimum time window before evaluating: ____
[ ] Soak time minimum between steps: ____ (policy enforced)

Safety checks:
[ ] Confirm auto-stop action is PAUSE by default (vs rollback), unless tenant policy requires rollback
[ ] Confirm rollback is a separate explicit action or only happens after pause + approval (depending on tier)
[ ] Confirm notifications route to correct internal channels for beta/GA (PagerDuty + Slack)

Runbook linkage:
[ ] Stop-condition fired path referenced in runbook (diagnostics, how to resume/rollback)

---

7) Approval gates / policy guardrails verification

Guardrails required for GA (PM-1851):
[ ] Max step size enforced (e.g., cannot jump from 5% to 100% unless policy allows)
[ ] Minimum soak time enforced between step promotions
[ ] Approval required for risky actions (configurable): start rollout, promote above threshold, rollback
[ ] Clear Console error messages on deny with “how to fix” guidance

RBAC behaviors:
[ ] Non-approver cannot approve steps / cannot override guardrails
[ ] Approver role can approve but still cannot exceed hard tenant policy caps
[ ] Audit events record actor, role, IP/user agent (as available), tenant, route, diffs

Edge cases to test (quick checklist):
[ ] Attempt to promote before soak time elapsed → denied, message displayed
[ ] Attempt step > max jump → denied
[ ] Attempt rollback without permission → denied
[ ] Attempt start while missing required metrics (no traffic) → allowed but stop conditions should not thrash

---

8) Release sequencing plan (staged enablement)

Stage 0 — Internal dogfood (already in progress)
[ ] Enable for Redwood internal tenant(s) only
[ ] Run 1–2 real rollouts of non-critical Hosted routes
[ ] Validate audit logs show up in internal audit viewer

Stage 1 — Design partner cohort (beta) stability check
[ ] Confirm no open P0/P1 issues from design partners tracker
[ ] Confirm support escalation path is active (#support-escalations + on-call)

Stage 2 — GA soft launch (allowlist)
Target: 10–20 tenants over first 48 hours
[ ] Enable tenant flag for first batch (coordinate w/ Support + PM)
[ ] Watch dashboards for 1 hour after each batch
[ ] Freeze further enablement if any routing correctness anomalies

Stage 3 — GA broad availability
[ ] Switch default enablement from allowlist → available-by-request → self-serve (per product decision)
[ ] Update support macros and internal enablement how-to

---

9) Backout / incident plan

Principle: Prefer “stop the bleeding” (disable enforcement) over partial rollbacks.

Backout levels (execute in this order for highest safety):

Level 1: Disable routing enforcement (fastest)
- Action: routing.hosted_route_canary_splitting = OFF
- Effect: all traffic goes to baseline routing behavior; rollouts remain visible but do not affect split
- Owner: SRE on-call
- Verification: canary cohort traffic drops to ~0% within 5–10 minutes; error rate normalizes

Level 2: Pause rollouts globally / block new rollouts
- Action: control_plane.hosted_canary_rollouts_orchestrator = allowlist-only OR “writes disabled” mode
- Effect: prevents new rollouts / step promotions; existing rollouts can be paused (manual)
- Owner: Control plane on-call

Level 3: Hide Console UI entry points
- Action: console.hosted_canary_rollouts_ui = OFF
- Effect: customers can’t initiate via Console; reduces load on support while investigation proceeds
- Owner: Release / Console on-call

Level 4: Full service rollback (last resort)
- Roll back orchestrator/routing builds only if a safe previous version is known-good and compatible with new schema.
- Requires: engineering leads approval (Dylan/Ethan/Mina) + SRE approval

Incident triggers (examples):
- Observed split mismatch > 2x expected sustained for > 15 minutes (e.g., config 10%, observed 30%)
- Cross-region inconsistency causing higher-than-expected canary traffic in a single region
- Auto-stop thrashing (pause/resume loops) affecting customer operations
- Audit logging failure for rollout actions (security regression)

Comms plan during incident:
[ ] Start internal incident channel (if Sev2+)
[ ] Notify Support lead (Dev Patel) and create/update customer comms snippet
[ ] For impacted enterprise tenants: direct CSM outreach

---

10) Verification tests (release-day run)

Staging:
[ ] Run E2E: create → start → 1% step → promote → pause → rollback → confirm baseline restored
[ ] Run E2E with approval required: start denied until approver approves
[ ] Force stop-condition breach in staging and verify auto-pause + notification

Production (internal tenant only):
[ ] Create rollout on a low-risk internal Hosted route
[ ] Confirm observed traffic split matches within tolerance (after warmup)
[ ] Confirm dashboards show baseline vs canary metrics with correct tags
[ ] Confirm audit events emitted and visible (and exportable if configured)

Post-enablement spot checks (first external tenants):
[ ] Confirm tenant can see rollout wizard + timeline
[ ] Confirm policy guardrails reflect tenant tier (max step, approvals)
[ ] Confirm support can retrieve rollout_id, state, and recent actions quickly

---

11) Documentation + support readiness

Customer docs:
[ ] “How to run a canary rollout” updated with screenshots and guardrail explanations
[ ] Troubleshooting section includes: split mismatch, auto-paused, stuck step, approval denied

Internal docs:
[ ] How-to enable feature for tenant is accurate and includes sanity checks
[ ] On-call runbook includes: diagnosing wrong split, disabling enforcement, checking cohort tags

Support enablement:
[ ] Support macro for “How do I do a percentage rollout?” includes current GA availability rules
[ ] Escalation template includes required fields: tenant_id, route_id, rollout_id, region, timestamps, expected %

---

- No multi-armed bandits / dynamic optimization
- Quality gates are optional/manual inputs only; not a blocking automated gate for GA
- Dedicated/Private parity not in GA scope; ensure schema compatibility only

    "title": "Hosted API: regional rollout safeguard playbook and automated rollback tooling",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-87209\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"Hosted API: regional rollout safeguard playbook and automated rollback tooling\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P0\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-01-12\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-02-05\",\n  \"creator\": \"Maya Patel\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Liam O'Connor\",\n  \"project\": \"runtime-rollouts\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2026-W02\",\n  \"estimate\": \"8\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2026-02-28\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"rollout\",\n    \"regional\",\n    \"slo\",\n    \"safety\",\n    \"automation\",\n    \"runbook\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-25401\",\n    \"ENG-21903\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"high\",\n  \"release\": \"hosted-api-2026.02\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"false\",\n  \"description\": \"Summary: Define and implement a tested, automated safeguard playbook for Hosted API regional rollouts that reduces blast radius and enables deterministic rollbacks. Deliverables: 1) a canonical rollout playbook (runbook) that combines blue/green cutover, progressive traffic tapering (attenuation curves), and SLO-driven gating; 2) automation to enact attenuation curves and instant circuit-breaker rollbacks via the orchestrator; 3) observability hooks and dashboards to make gating decisions actionable; 4) a post-incident checklist and a DR rehearsal plan.\\n\\nBackground: We continue to see subtle regressions surface only at regional scale during fast rollouts (latency spikes, 5xx bursts tied to model variant memory behavior, or upstream rate-limiter thrash). Current manual tactics (manual weight changes + Slack coordination) are slow and error-prone for multi-region blue/green swaps. This ticket hardens the pipeline so rollouts are reproducible, reversible, and constrained by SLO/health signals.\\n\\nGoals: - Reduce mean time to rollback from minutes of manual coordination to < 90s automated action (trigger + rollback). - Limit customer impact by enforcing an initial stagger window and automated attenuation curve (e.g., 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with safety holdpoints). - Ensure rollouts respect per-route token-latency and error-budget thresholds; if threshold crossed, hold and/or rollback. - Provide a runbook and automation that can be run for Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private (config flags for environment differences).\\n\\nAcceptance criteria: - Playbook doc in Confluence linked from ticket and Console Runbooks section. - Orchestrator accepts an attenuation profile and regional schedule and performs the weight shifts automatically. - Two independent gating signals implemented: (a) SLO-based (p90 latency > configured threshold or error-rate > configured threshold) and (b) resource-based (GPU utilization / mem pressure exceeding setpoint). - Automatic rollback executes a safe drain and traffic rehoming with no more than 10% request loss over a 5m window in canary/initial stages. - End-to-end integration test that simulates failures and validates automation triggers a rollback. - Dashboard tiles in Console for rollout progress, per-region health, and per-route SLOs.\\n\\nImplementation notes: - Attenuation curves are parameterized objects: initial_percentage, step_multiplier, max_step, hold_minutes. The orchestrator will at runtime compute ramp steps and schedule weight shifts. - Rollback semantics: when a gate trips, the controller first attempts a tapered drain back to the previous active set (blue) with prioritized draining for warm KV-cache sessions; if drain fails due to resource pressure, escalate to immediate regional failover to previous model variant. - Health signals are aggregated at 10s cadence with 3-window exponential backoff for noisy signals. Gate evaluation uses a sliding-window error budget that factors in traffic weight to avoid overreacting to low-volume noise. - Integrations: Console (dashboards + approval UI), Tracing service (link traces to rollout tiles), PagerDuty + Slack for escalations, and GitHub for audit (rollout automation posts PR/commit refs).\\n\\nTesting plan: - Unit tests for attenuation logic. - Integration test harness that can replay recorded workload traces and emulate regional degradation (latency/error injection). - Chaos test: synthetic 5xx burst injected during a staged rollout to assert hold and rollback. - DR rehearsal: simulate cross-region outage and validate automated failover.\\n\\nRunbook highlights (linked artifacts below): - Pre-rollout checklist: validate model artifact hashes, probing endpoints, baseline SLO snapshot, and smoke test on a canary route. - During rollout: monitor the rollout tile, watchgate timers, and console approval prompt (if manual hold enabled). - On gate trip: follow automated rollback steps; if automation cannot complete within 90s, engage manual oncall with the emergency rollback play. - Post-rollback: collect logs, capture heap/memory profile, annotate PRs and release notes, schedule postmortem if customer impact > low.\\n\\nRisk/Tradeoffs: - More aggressive automation reduces time-to-rollback but increases chance of incorrect rollbacks due to false-positive signals; mitigations include multi-signal gating and traffic-weight aware thresholds. - Extra orchestration complexity increases surface area; we'll incrementally release automation behind a feature flag and limit to internal canaries first.\\n\\nLinks and artifacts: - Playbook (confluence): https://confluence.internal.redwood.com/display/RUNTIME/Regional+Rollout+Safeguard+Playbook - Design doc (drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1rOLpExampleDesignDoc - Orchestrator PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4123 - Auto-rollback worker PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4187 - Integration tests: https://github.com/redwood/repo/tree/main/integration/rollout-harness - Console dashboard prototype: https://console.internal.redwood.com/dashboards/rollouts/87209 - Incident learning reference: https://wiki.internal.redwood.com/incidents/2025-09-regional-latency\",\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2026-01-12 - Maya Patel: Created ticket after postmortem for 2025-09 regional latency incident. Initial scope approved by Runtime PM. Proposed attenuation curve parameters and gating signals included in design doc.\",\n    \"2026-01-18 - Liam O'Connor: Spike complete for attenuation algorithm. Implemented scheduler prototype and validated ramp math with synthetic traffic. Results attached to PR #4123.\",\n    \"2026-01-22 - SRE Review (Aisha Rahman): Suggested increasing health-signal aggregation cadence to 10s and adding a second signal for GPU mem high-water. Also recommended feature flagging the automation.\",\n    \"2026-01-29 - QA (Diego Alvarez): Integration harness can simulate 5xx bursts and asserted that automated hold occurs at 20% weight during tests. Noted flakiness when traffic < 0.5% leading to noisy metrics; added traffic-weight threshold check.\",\n    \"2026-02-03 - Security (Priya Nair): Reviewed runbook for audit trail needs. Requested automatic audit entries for each weight shift (GitHub comment + console event). Security review concluded no extra controls required.\",\n    \"2026-02-05 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented basic rollback worker and wiring. Next: add draining prioritization for KV-hot sessions and schedule a rehearsal with Platform team on 2026-02-18.\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"comments\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_a4b927b2fb2f45cb97bddda127a2cb37\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API: regional rollout safeguard playbook and automated rollback tooling\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-87209-hosted-api-regional-traffic-safeguard-playbook.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: runtime-rollouts\nTeam: engineering\n\ndashboards to make gating decisions actionable ; 4 ) a post - incident checklist and a dr rehearsal plan. background : we continue to see subtle regressions surface only at regional scale during fast rollouts ( latency spikes, 5xx bursts tied to model variant memory behavior, or upstream rate - limiter thrash ). current manual tactics ( manual weight changes + slack coordination ) are slow and error - prone for multi - region blue / green swaps. this ticket hardens the pipeline so rollouts are reproducible, reversible, and constrained by slo / health signals.",

      "ordinal": 3,
      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API: regional rollout safeguard playbook and automated rollback tooling\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-87209-hosted-api-regional-traffic-safeguard-playbook.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: runtime-rollouts\nTeam: engineering\n\n##s the pipeline so rollouts are reproducible, reversible, and constrained by slo / health signals. goals : - reduce mean time to rollback from minutes of manual coordination to < 90s automated action ( trigger + rollback ). - limit customer impact by enforcing an initial stagger window and automated attenuation curve ( e. g., 1 % - > 5 % - > 20 % - > 50 % - > 100 % with safety holdpoints ). - ensure rollouts respect per - route token - latency and error - budget thresholds ; if threshold crossed, hold and / or rollback. - provide a runbook and automation that can be run for hosted api, dedicated, and private ( config flags for environment differences ).",

document.content:
{
  "key": "ENG-87209",
  "team": "engineering",
  "title": "Hosted API: regional rollout safeguard playbook and automated rollback tooling",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P0",
  "created_at": "2026-01-12",
  "updated_at": "2026-02-05",
  "creator": "Maya Patel",
  "assignee": "Liam O'Connor",
  "project": "runtime-rollouts",
  "cycle": "2026-W02",
  "estimate": "8",
  "due_date": "2026-02-28",
  "labels": [
    "rollout",
    "regional",
    "slo",
    "safety",
    "automation",
    "runbook"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-25401",
    "ENG-21903"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "high",
  "release": "hosted-api-2026.02",
  "security_review_required": "false",
  "description": "Summary: Define and implement a tested, automated safeguard playbook for Hosted API regional rollouts that reduces blast radius and enables deterministic rollbacks. Deliverables: 1) a canonical rollout playbook (runbook) that combines blue/green cutover, progressive traffic tapering (attenuation curves), and SLO-driven gating; 2) automation to enact attenuation curves and instant circuit-breaker rollbacks via the orchestrator; 3) observability hooks and dashboards to make gating decisions actionable; 4) a post-incident checklist and a DR rehearsal plan.\n\nBackground: We continue to see subtle regressions surface only at regional scale during fast rollouts (latency spikes, 5xx bursts tied to model variant memory behavior, or upstream rate-limiter thrash). Current manual tactics (manual weight changes + Slack coordination) are slow and error-prone for multi-region blue/green swaps. This ticket hardens the pipeline so rollouts are reproducible, reversible, and constrained by SLO/health signals.\n\nGoals: - Reduce mean time to rollback from minutes of manual coordination to < 90s automated action (trigger + rollback). - Limit customer impact by enforcing an initial stagger window and automated attenuation curve (e.g., 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with safety holdpoints). - Ensure rollouts respect per-route token-latency and error-budget thresholds; if threshold crossed, hold and/or rollback. - Provide a runbook and automation that can be run for Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private (config flags for environment differences).\n\nAcceptance criteria: - Playbook doc in Confluence linked from ticket and Console Runbooks section. - Orchestrator accepts an attenuation profile and regional schedule and performs the weight shifts automatically. - Two independent gating signals implemented: (a) SLO-based (p90 latency > configured threshold or error-rate > configured threshold) and (b) resource-based (GPU utilization / mem pressure exceeding setpoint). - Automatic rollback executes a safe drain and traffic rehoming with no more than 10% request loss over a 5m window in canary/initial stages. - End-to-end integration test that simulates failures and validates automation triggers a rollback. - Dashboard tiles in Console for rollout progress, per-region health, and per-route SLOs.\n\nImplementation notes: - Attenuation curves are parameterized objects: initial_percentage, step_multiplier, max_step, hold_minutes. The orchestrator will at runtime compute ramp steps and schedule weight shifts. - Rollback semantics: when a gate trips, the controller first attempts a tapered drain back to the previous active set (blue) with prioritized draining for warm KV-cache sessions; if drain fails due to resource pressure, escalate to immediate regional failover to previous model variant. - Health signals are aggregated at 10s cadence with 3-window exponential backoff for noisy signals. Gate evaluation uses a sliding-window error budget that factors in traffic weight to avoid overreacting to low-volume noise. - Integrations: Console (dashboards + approval UI), Tracing service (link traces to rollout tiles), PagerDuty + Slack for escalations, and GitHub for audit (rollout automation posts PR/commit refs).\n\nTesting plan: - Unit tests for attenuation logic. - Integration test harness that can replay recorded workload traces and emulate regional degradation (latency/error injection). - Chaos test: synthetic 5xx burst injected during a staged rollout to assert hold and rollback. - DR rehearsal: simulate cross-region outage and validate automated failover.\n\nRunbook highlights (linked artifacts below): - Pre-rollout checklist: validate model artifact hashes, probing endpoints, baseline SLO snapshot, and smoke test on a canary route. - During rollout: monitor the rollout tile, watchgate timers, and console approval prompt (if manual hold enabled). - On gate trip: follow automated rollback steps; if automation cannot complete within 90s, engage manual oncall with the emergency rollback play. - Post-rollback: collect logs, capture heap/memory profile, annotate PRs and release notes, schedule postmortem if customer impact > low.\n\nRisk/Tradeoffs: - More aggressive automation reduces time-to-rollback but increases chance of incorrect rollbacks due to false-positive signals; mitigations include multi-signal gating and traffic-weight aware thresholds. - Extra orchestration complexity increases surface area; we'll incrementally release automation behind a feature flag and limit to internal canaries first.\n\nLinks and artifacts: - Playbook (confluence): https://confluence.internal.redwood.com/display/RUNTIME/Regional+Rollout+Safeguard+Playbook - Design doc (drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1rOLpExampleDesignDoc - Orchestrator PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4123 - Auto-rollback worker PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4187 - Integration tests: https://github.com/redwood/repo/tree/main/integration/rollout-harness - Console dashboard prototype: https://console.internal.redwood.com/dashboards/rollouts/87209 - Incident learning reference: https://wiki.internal.redwood.com/incidents/2025-09-regional-latency",
  "comments": [
    "2026-01-12 - Maya Patel: Created ticket after postmortem for 2025-09 regional latency incident. Initial scope approved by Runtime PM. Proposed attenuation curve parameters and gating signals included in design doc.",
    "2026-01-18 - Liam O'Connor: Spike complete for attenuation algorithm. Implemented scheduler prototype and validated ramp math with synthetic traffic. Results attached to PR #4123.",
    "2026-01-22 - SRE Review (Aisha Rahman): Suggested increasing health-signal aggregation cadence to 10s and adding a second signal for GPU mem high-water. Also recommended feature flagging the automation.",
    "2026-01-29 - QA (Diego Alvarez): Integration harness can simulate 5xx bursts and asserted that automated hold occurs at 20% weight during tests. Noted flakiness when traffic < 0.5% leading to noisy metrics; added traffic-weight threshold check.",
    "2026-02-03 - Security (Priya Nair): Reviewed runbook for audit trail needs. Requested automatic audit entries for each weight shift (GitHub comment + console event). Security review concluded no extra controls required.",
    "2026-02-05 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented basic rollback worker and wiring. Next: add draining prioritization for KV-hot sessions and schedule a rehearsal with Platform team on 2026-02-18."
  ],
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "comments"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_a4b927b2fb2f45cb97bddda127a2cb37"
}

# Hosted API launch readiness

Owner: Ethan Park, Platform & Console
Decision status: Evidence review in progress (operational reconciliation complete)

## Proposed capability and supported launch shape

Launch a staged public Hosted API surface for chat, completions, embeddings (single and batches up to 8), and server-side rerank. The contract is REST/OpenAPI, versioned and backward-compatible; core JS/Python SDKs, API-key/OAuth2 authentication, tier-aware quotas, retry guidance, structured chat output, streaming/SSE, deterministic embeddings, and stable rerank semantics are in scope. Dedicated/private deployment bundles and full non-core SDK parity remain out of scope. [PM-80421; dsid_6f6a548d740249f6a1413a8ab778f270; /knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/PM-80421-hosted-api-capability-prioritization-acceptance-rollout.json]

Operational evidence narrows the safe initial exposure to per-tenant allowlisted Hosted routes, internal dogfood first, then a design-partner cohort and 10–20-tenant soft launch, with broad availability only after the gates below pass. [dsid_fa0fb79e2f54457093ad3f831e7ac6a2; /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/hosted-canary-ga-change-management-checklist.json]

## Gates already supported by evidence

- Product scope, non-goals, endpoint behavior, versioning, telemetry, SLO targets, rollout stages, and quantitative PRD canary stop conditions are defined.
- Console flows received design review; explicit streaming-interruption error states remain a requested closure item.
- Rerank is intentionally a dedicated route to reduce autoscaler and tail-latency risk.
- The published 2026 SRE policy defines Hosted multi-region availability at 99.95% over a rolling 30-day window for paid, multi-region-eligible routes, with multi-window burn alerts and an SRE-review/change-freeze policy when error-budget consumption is high.
- The regional safeguard design has a working attenuation scheduler prototype and failure-injection harness; Security concluded no extra control beyond automatic weight-shift audit entries for that safeguard.

Product/design: [PM-80421; dsid_6f6a548d740249f6a1413a8ab778f270; /knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/PM-80421-hosted-api-capability-prioritization-acceptance-rollout.json]. [Document context]
Title: Hosted API Launch Readiness
Source: Ethan Park launch readiness review
Path: /artifacts/product/launch-readiness.md
Workspace: task/ethan-park/launch-readiness-v2

# Hosted API launch readiness

Owner: Ethan Park, Platform & Console
Decision status: Evidence review in progress (operational reconciliation complete)

## Proposed capability and supported launch shape

Launch a staged public Hosted API surface for chat, completions, embeddings (single and batches up to 8), and server-side rerank. The contract is REST/OpenAPI, versioned and backward-compatible; core JS/Python SDKs, API-key/OAuth2 authentication, tier-aware quotas, retry guidance, structured chat output, streaming/SSE, deterministic embeddings, and stable rerank semantics are in scope. Dedicated/private deployment bundles and full non-core SDK parity remain out of scope. [PM-80421; dsid_6f6a548d740249f6a1413a8ab778f270; /knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/PM-80421-hosted-api-capability-prioritization-acceptance-rollout.json]

Operational evidence narrows the safe initial exposure to per-tenant allowlisted Hosted routes, internal dogfood first, then a design-partner cohort and 10–20-tenant soft launch, with broad availability only after the gates below pass. [dsid_fa0fb79e2f54457093ad3f831e7ac6a2; /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/hosted-canary-ga-change-management-checklist.json]

## Gates already supported by evidence

# Hosted API launch readiness

Owner: Ethan Park, Platform & Console
Decision status: Evidence review in progress (operational reconciliation complete)

## Proposed capability and supported launch shape

Launch a staged public Hosted API surface for chat, completions, embeddings (single and batches up to 8), and server-side rerank. The contract is REST/OpenAPI, versioned and backward-compatible; core JS/Python SDKs, API-key/OAuth2 authentication, tier-aware quotas, retry guidance, structured chat output, streaming/SSE, deterministic embeddings, and stable rerank semantics are in scope. Dedicated/private deployment bundles and full non-core SDK parity remain out of scope. {
  "title": "Beta design partners tracker \u2014 Hosted canary rollouts (GA workflow)",
  "owner": "Simran Kaur",
  "drive_area": "shared_drives",
  "path": "shared_drives/product/console-and-rollouts/beta-design-partners-tracker-hosted-canary.json",
  "doc_type": "sheet",
  "created_at": "2025-03-06",
  "last_modified": "2025-05-02",
  "collaborators": [
    "Marissa Cole",
    "Paula Mendes",
    "Dylan Brooks",
    "Sean Gallagher",
    "Dev Patel",
    "Talia Benson"
  ],
  "team": "product-console-rollouts",
  "status": "in_review",
  "tags": [
    "hosted",
    "canary",
    "rollouts",
    "beta",
    "design-partners",
    "ga-readiness",
    "console",
    "policy-guardrails",
    "telemetry",
    "audit-logs"
  ],
  "linked_artifacts": [
    "Linear: PM-1843",
    "Linear: PM-1859",
    "Linear: ENG-9123",
    "Linear: ENG-9158",
    "Slack: incidents/1740726110-rollout-split-mismatch-us-east",
    "GitHub: redwood/pr-28895-fix-rollout-step-stuck-on-metric-timeout",
    "GitHub: redwood/pr-28877-rollout-activity-log-and-audit-events",
    "Jira: SUP-48377"
  ],
  "content": "Last updated: 2025-05-02 (Simran)\n\nPurpose\n- Working tracker for Hosted canary rollout workflow beta design partners.\n- We\u2019re using this to drive: enablement sequencing, feedback capture, GA readiness signal, and comms.\n\nLegend\n- Readiness: \u2705 Ready for GA / \ud83d\udfe1 Conditional / \u274c Not ready\n- Severity: P0 = customer-impacting incident, P1 = blocks rollout workflow, P2 = significant UX/paper cut, P3 = nice-to-have\n- \u201cRoutes involved\u201d refers to Hosted routes in Console (route name) + API path (if applicable)\n\nNotes / reminders\n- Please keep \u201cIssues found\u201d short + link to Jira/Linear/Slack where possible.\n- If a customer requests a feature outside GA scope (quality gates automation, Dedicated parity), capture in \u201cFollow-ups\u201d with owner.\n\nTable (sheet export)\nPartner\tSegment\tPrimary contact (DP)\tEnablement (tenant flag)\tFirst rollout started\tRoutes involved\tBaseline \u2192 Canary\tTraffic schedule used\tGuardrails config used\tSuccess criteria (DP-specific)\tWhat we learned\tIssues found (w/ severity)\tWorkarounds used\tCurrent status\tReadiness for GA\tCan be public reference?\tFollow-ups / owner\nNorthstar Support AI\tAI-native SaaS (support agent)\tSimran Kaur\t2025-03-12\t2025-03-14\tprod-support-chat (/v1/chat/completions)\tllama-3.1-70b-instruct:v2025-02-28 \u2192 v2025-03-10 (same model, new quant profile)\t1%\u21925%\u219225%\u219250%\u2192100% (2h soak)\tMax step=25%; Min soak=60m; Approvals=none; Auto-stop: 5xx>1.0% (5m) OR p95 latency +30% (10m)\t(1) No >0.2% increase in timeouts; (2) p95 latency within +20% at 50%; (3) rollback <2 min; (4) clear UI timeline for exec review\tAuto-stop defaults are a bit \u201ctwitchy\u201d for bursty traffic; metrics compare view was heavily used (p95 + error overlays); they want \u201cexplain why paused\u201d copy to be more explicit\tP1: Rollout auto-paused on brief latency spike (threshold too sensitive) \u2014 SUP-48302; P2: Wizard copy unclear on \u201cbaseline pinned version\u201d (confused about fallback)\tTemporarily raised p95 regression threshold to +45% during peak hours; added manual approval step in internal process (not product)\tCompleted 3 rollouts (2 successful, 1 rollback). No open blockers.\t\u2705 Ready for GA\tYes (logo ok after GA)\t(1) Product: add \u201cpause reason\u201d detail drawer (Marissa/Tessa); (2) SRE: recommend tier-based default thresholds (Sean/Paula)\nEmberfin\tRegulated fintech\tSimran Kaur\t2025-03-26\t2025-03-28\tclaims-assist-chat (/v1/chat/completions)\tqwen2.5-72b-instruct:v2025-03-01 \u2192 v2025-03-20 (new system prompt + model patch)\t1%\u21925%\u219210% (24h soak; paused before 25%)\tMax step=10%; Min soak=12h; Approvals=Required (rollout-approver role); Auto-stop: 5xx>0.5% (10m) OR timeouts>0.2% (10m)\t(1) Approval/audit trail meets governance; (2) clear \u201cwho approved what\u201d export; (3) can pause outside business hours; (4) no cross-region variance surprises\tApproval gates were a strong positive; they asked about audit log retention + SIEM export (we pointed to internal spec but want customer-facing doc snippet). They also want \u201cchange diff\u201d to include guardrail edits and traffic schedule edits in one view.\tP1: Audit export fields not consistent across events (missing route_id in one event type) \u2014 raised to Marcus/Kevin; P2: Confusion: approver role needed to \u201cresume\u201d after auto-pause (policy error message too generic)\tManual export from Console activity timeline; SRE assisted verifying events via internal audit stream\tPaused at 10% pending audit export clarification + policy error message fix\t\ud83d\udfe1 Conditional\tNo (security posture) until Q3\t(1) Security: confirm final audit event schema + doc excerpt (Marcus/Wei); (2) Policy: improve deny message and surface \u201crequired role\u201d (Jordan/Chloe)\nAurumHR\tMid-market HR SaaS\tSimran Kaur\t2025-04-03\t2025-04-04\tcandidate-screening (/v1/chat/completions)\tllama-3.1-8b-instruct:v2025-03-15 \u2192 v2025-04-01 (new runtime batching settings)\t5%\u219225%\u219250%\u2192100% (1h soak)\tMax step=25%; Min soak=30m; Approvals=none; Auto-stop: 5xx>1.5% (5m) OR p95 +40% (10m)\t(1) Improve cost per 1k tokens by 10% without hurting p95 > +15%; (2) at least 2 successful rollouts without Redwood help\tThey mainly used canary to validate new performance config; appreciated \u201cpreview plan\u201d summary. Requested a \u201ccost delta\u201d widget in cohort compare view.\tP2: Metrics compare view loads slowly when filtering by region+route (dashboard query); P3: Wants cost comparison across cohorts on same screen\tUsed fewer dimensions (no region filter) to speed charts\t2 successful rollouts; continuing to use monthly\t\u2705 Ready for GA\tMaybe (pending marketing approval)\t(1) Observability: optimize compare query defaults (Thomas/Felix); (2) Product: add \u201ctoken cost delta\u201d follow-up (Paula/Marissa)\nDocuSage\tEnterprise knowledge mgmt\tSimran Kaur\t2025-04-09\t2025-04-11\tdocusage-assistant (/v1/chat/completions)\tmistral-large-2:v2025-03-22 \u2192 v2025-04-05 (new safety filters)\t1%\u21925%\u219225% (4h soak)\tMax step=25%; Min soak=2h; Approvals=optional; Auto-stop: 5xx>1.0% (5m) OR p95 +30% (10m) OR streaming disconnects >0.3%\t(1) No increase in streaming disconnects; (2) rollback preserves sticky sessions; (3) regions: us-east + eu-west behave similarly\tStreaming-specific stop condition was valuable; they validated cohort stickiness with retries (wanted deterministic behavior). Asked for a doc section on \u201cstickiness + retries + streaming\u201d\tP0: Traffic split mismatch observed in us-east during step 25% (canary got ~40% for ~12 min) \u2014 Slack incident 1740726110 + SUP-48377; fixed in PR-28895 / routing mitigation deployed\tTemporarily forced 0% canary via kill switch; re-ran rollout after fix\tCompleted rollout after fix; monitoring for recurrence\t\u2705 Ready for GA (with fix)\tNo\t(1) Docs: add streaming/retry/stickiness explanation (Wei/Elliot); (2) SRE: add \u201csplit mismatch\u201d diagnostic steps to runbook (Rafael)\nHelioTravel\tConsumer travel (high traffic spikes)\tSimran Kaur\t2025-04-16\t2025-04-18\ttrip-planner (/v1/chat/completions)\tllama-3.1-70b-instruct:v2025-03-30 \u2192 v2025-04-12 (prompt + tool schema changes)\t1%\u21925%\u219225% (auto-paused twice)\tMax step=20%; Min soak=1h; Approvals=none; Auto-stop: 5xx>1.0% (5m) OR p95 +25% (10m)\t(1) Better tool-call reliability; (2) avoid false-positive auto-pauses during known burst windows; (3) must be able to schedule steps around traffic\tThey want \u201cmaintenance window / schedule step at time\u201d (not GA). Confirmed that default thresholds need guidance for bursty workloads. They liked review screen.\tP2: Policy denial messaging too generic (same as Emberfin); P3: Wants email notification on approval requested\tUsed Slack + internal process for approval request notification\tCompleted rollout successfully\t\u2705 Ready for GA\tYes (case study possible)\t(1) Policy: actionable denial messages (Jordan/Chloe); (2) Notifications backlog (Dylan)\n\nRollup (non-binding)\n- Total DPs enabled: 6\n- Actively running/used rollouts: 6\n- \u201c\u2705 Ready for GA\u201d signals: 4 (Northstar, AurumHR, DocuSage, Canyon)\n- \u201c\ud83d\udfe1 Conditional\u201d signals: 2 (Emberfin = audit/policy messaging; HelioTravel = threshold guidance + burst handling)\n\nTop recurring themes (what to fix / clarify before GA)\n1) Auto-stop/rollback defaults need better guidance + tier recommendations (bursty traffic = false positives)\n2) Policy denial messaging must say: what rule tripped + required role/action (resume/approve)\n3) Audit events: consistency + ensure route_id/rollout_id/cohort + \u201cdiff\u201d completeness (guardrail edits + schedule edits)\n4) Split mismatch runbook + verification steps should be easy to follow (post-incident)\n\nOpen questions (captured from calls)\n- Do we recommend a standard \u201csoak time by step\u201d default per traffic volume? (GA)\\n- Hosted routes only (Dedicated/Private: schema-compatible, not GA)\\n- Console wizard to create/run/pause/rollback, plus timeline/activity view and cohort comparison metrics\\n- Policy events present for all required action types, with correct actor identity and diffs.\\n\\nGA Launch Checklist (go/no-go)\\nA) Functional completeness (Console + API)\\nOwner: Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin\\n- Wizard flow supports:\\n  - Selecting route, baseline model version/config, canary model version/config\\n  - Defining traffic schedule (step %, soak duration)\\n  - Configuring guardrails (max step size, min soak time) and showing validation errors clearly\\n  - Review + confirm with explicit warnings for destructive actions (rollback)\\n- Lifecycle actions supported and validated end-to-end:\\n  - Create rollout (draft)\\n  - Start rollout\\n  - Progress to next step (with/without approval gate)\\n  - Pause/resume\\n  - Rollback (manual) and \\u201crollback to baseline\\u201d semantics\\n  - Auto-pause / auto-rollback on SLO breach (with reason surfaced)\\n- State machine correctness:\\n  - No \\u201cstuck\\u201d states on metric evaluation timeouts; clear retry + user-facing error\\n  - Idempotent retries for control plane \\u2192 data plane propagation\\n- API parity for core operations (documented): create, get status, list activity, approve step, pause/resume, rollback\\n\\nAcceptance evidence\\n- E2E test suite passing in CI and nightly (ENG-9164)\\n- Staging manual walkthrough recorded (link in go/no-go notes)\\n\\nB) Smart Routing enforcement correctness\\nOwner: Mina Haddad / Ravi Menon\\n- Deterministic cohorting implemented and documented (hash inputs + stickiness rules)\\n- Percentage split accuracy within tolerance per region (define tolerance below)\\n- Correct behavior for:\\n  - Multi-region traffic\\n  - Streaming requests\\n  - Retries (client and internal)\\n  - Fallback routing interactions (baseline vs canary; precedence per ADR)\\n- Kill switch behavior verified:\\n  - Tenant-level disable immediately forces 100% baseline\\n  - Global disable forces baseline and prevents new rollouts from starting\\n\\nSplit accuracy target (GA)\\n- For stable traffic volume, measured canary proportion should converge to target within \\u00b12% absolute over a 15-minute window (per region), excluding low-volume routes.\\n- For low volume routes, UI must display \\u201cinsufficient volume\\u201d guidance instead of implying precise percentages.\\n\\nAcceptance evidence\\n- Staging smoke tests (perf-canary PR-147)\\n- Post-fix validation for beta split mismatch scenario (see incident thread: rollout-split-mismatch-us-east)\\n\\nC) Telemetry, dashboards, and alerting\\nOwner: Sean Gallagher / Aisha Bello / Logan Wright\\nRequired cohort signals (tagging + aggregation)\\n- Every request must be attributable to:\\n  - route\\n  - model version/config (baseline vs canary)\\n  - cohort (baseline/canary)\\n  - region\\n  - rollout_id (with cardinality controls; ensure no blowups)\\n- Metrics required in Console comparison view + internal dashboards:\\n  - Request rate (RPS)\\n  - Error rate (overall, 5xx, timeouts)\\n  - Latency (p50/p95; ideally p99 in internal)\\n  - Tokens/sec and cost proxies (where available)\\n  - Streaming-specific failure modes (disconnects, partial completions) if tracked\\n\\nStop conditions (GA defaults)\\n- Auto-stop/auto-rollback must be available and enabled by default for new rollouts (with ability to tune thresholds by entitlement/tier).\\n- Default thresholds (initial GA proposal; finalize with SRE):\\n  - 5xx error rate: canary exceeds baseline by +1.0% absolute AND exceeds 2.0% absolute for 5 minutes\\n  - Timeout rate: canary exceeds baseline by +0.5% absolute for 5 minutes\\n  - p95 latency regression: canary p95 > baseline p95 * 1.25 for 10 minutes (guard for low volume)\\n- Rollout behavior on breach:\\n  - Auto-pause first if we can attribute breach confidently; auto-rollback when breach persists (or per policy)\\n  - Always emit: (1) customer-visible timeline entry, (2) audit event, (3) notification event\\n\\nAlerting guidelines\\n- Alerts should page SRE only for:\\n  - Routing enforcement drift/incorrectness\\n  - Orchestrator stuck rollouts at scale\\n  - Global cohort tagging failures\\n  - Control plane \\u2192 data plane propagation failures\\n- Customer route-specific canary SLO breaches should notify customer in Console/timeline and optionally via webhook/email (no paging unless systemic).\\n\\nAcceptance evidence\\n- Cohort dashboards exist + validated against known traffic patterns (PR-28910 / observability pack PR-184)\\n- Cardinality analysis completed and within limits (Drive: rollout-cohort-metrics-cardinality-analysis)\\n\\nD) Audit logging + change history (Security/Compliance)\\nOwner: Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei\\nRequired audit event coverage\\n- Events must be emitted for:\\n  - rollout.created\\n  - rollout.started\\n  - rollout.step.approval_requested\\n  - rollout.step.approved / rollout.step.denied\\n  - rollout.step.changed (percent change)\\n  - rollout.paused / rollout.resumed\\n  - rollout.rolled_back (manual)\\n  - rollout.auto_paused / rollout.auto_rolled_back (include stop condition + metric snapshot reference)\\n  - rollout.completed\\n- Required fields (high level): tenant_id, actor_id/actor_type, route_id, rollout_id, previous_state \\u2192 new_state, diff (human readable + structured), timestamp, request_id/trace_id when applicable.\\n- Retention and export:\\n  - Align with existing audit log retention policy by tier\\n  - Verify SIEM export compatibility (field naming and size limits)\\n\\nCustomer-visible activity timeline\\n- Must match audit events but may exclude security-only internal fields; should show \\u201cwhat happened\\u201d and \\u201cwhy\\u201d (e.g., auto-pause reason).\\n\\nAcceptance evidence\\n- Security review of audit event schema doc (Confluence: audit-events-rollout-actions)\\n- Sample events captured in staging and validated by Security (screenshots/log dumps referenced in go/no-go)\\n\\nE) Policy guardrails + RBAC\\nOwner: Jordan Lee / Kaitlyn Nguyen\\n- Guardrails enforced for step changes:\\n  - Max step size (e.g., 1% \\u2192 50% disallowed without override/approval)\\n  - Minimum soak time before next step\\n  - Approval gates configurable by tenant/admin policy\\n- Entitlement mapping documented:\\n  - Which customers get auto-rollback, approvals, advanced retention, etc.\\n- RBAC roles validated:\\n  - Who can create rollouts\\n  - Who can start/pause/rollback\\n  - Who can approve (rollout-approver role)\\n- UI error messaging must reflect policy engine errors with actionable guidance (e.g., \\u201cWait 20m more to satisfy min soak\\u201d)\\n\\nAcceptance evidence\\n- Policy engine tests and Console integration tests pass (PR-28802)\\n- Manual validation with at least 2 common enterprise role setups\\n\\nF) Documentation (public + internal)\\nOwner: Elliot Price / Wei Chen\\nCustomer docs must include\\n- Conceptual overview: baseline vs canary, cohorting, step schedule, soak time\\n- Step-by-step Console walkthrough\\n- API reference (or links) for rollout operations\\n- Troubleshooting:\\n  - Why a rollout auto-paused\\n  - Why metrics show \\u201cinsufficient volume\\u201d\\n  - Split mismatch debugging steps (what to check before contacting support)\\n  - How to rollback safely\\n- Limitations (GA):\\n  - No bandits/dynamic optimization\\n  - Quality gates optional/manual (not hard gates)\\n  - Dedicated/Private not GA\\n\\nInternal docs must include\\n- Enablement how-to (feature flags, permissions, sanity checks)\\n- On-call runbook for stuck rollout / bad split\\n- Release/change management checklist\\n\\nAcceptance evidence\\n- Docs PR merged (redwood-docs PR-922)\\n- Runbooks published (Confluence) and reviewed with SRE + Support\\n\\nG) Support readiness + incident response\\nOwner: Dev Patel / Rafael Mendes\\n- Support playbooks:\\n  - Triage flow for \\u201crollout paused unexpectedly after latency spike\\u201d\\n  - Triage flow for \\u201ctraffic split not matching config\\u201d\\n  - Escalation path to on-call / engineering\\n  - What data to request: tenant_id, route, rollout_id, timeframe, region, request IDs\\n- Macros/snippets created for common questions (e.g., \\u201cHow do I do a percentage rollout on Hosted route?\\u201d)\\n- SLA for response during GA launch week and ownership for escalation channel\\n\\nAcceptance evidence\\n- At least 2 support training sessions run (recording link in go/no-go)\\n- Sample tickets resolved using new macros (reference: SUP-48211, SUP-48302, SUP-48377)\\n\\nH) Release management + staged rollout plan\\nOwner: Connor O'Brien / Soojin Lee\\n- Feature flags:\\n  - Per-tenant enablement\\n  - Internal dogfood tenants first\\n  - Staged cohort of beta \\u2192 expanded beta \\u2192 GA default (if applicable)\\n  - Kill switch playbook (owners + steps)\\n- Migration/backward compatibility validated for config schema changes\\n- Backout strategy:\\n  - Disable canary UI\\n  - Force baseline routing\\n  - Preserve audit logs and rollout history for completed rollouts\\n\\nAcceptance evidence\\n- Change management checklist completed (Drive: hosted-canary-ga-change-management-checklist)\\n- Release readiness review held 48\\u201372 hours pre-GA\\n\\nGo/No-Go Process (how we decide)\\nMeeting: GA Readiness Review (60 minutes)\\nRequired attendees / signoffs\\n- Product: Marissa Cole (final call)\\n- Console Eng: Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin\\n- Platform/Policy: Ethan Park / Jordan Lee\\n- Smart Routing: Mina Haddad\\n- SRE: Sean Gallagher or Rafael Mendes\\n- Security: Marcus Lin\\n- Docs/Support: Elliot Price + Dev Patel\\n\\nDecision rules\\n- No-go if any of:\\n  - Known issue causing incorrect split enforcement at material rates\\n  - Rollback unavailable or unreliable\\n  - Missing audit events for any action type listed above\\n  - Unbounded metrics cardinality risk unresolved\\n  - No validated kill switch\\n- Conditional go allowed if:\\n  - Minor UI polish issues only\\n  - Non-blocking docs follow-ups with explicit owner + date\\n  - Non-paging alert tuning improvements queued (does not impact safety)\\n\\nArtifacts to attach in go/no-go notes\\n- Links: PRD, design spec, ADRs\\n- Latest beta partner tracker snapshot\\n- List of open bugs (P0/P1 only) with owners + ETA\\n- Staging game day results + any follow-ups\\n\\nCurrent status / open questions (as of last update)\\n- Need final agreement on GA default thresholds by region/tier; beta feedback suggests p95 multiplier threshold may be too aggressive for long-context routes.\\n- Confirm whether GA requires customer notifications beyond Console timeline (e.g., webhook). If not in GA, docs must state Console-only.\\n- Ensure \\u201cinsufficient volume\\u201d guidance text matches design copy and does not confuse customers about split accuracy.\\n\\nLinks\\n- Confluence PRD: hosted-canary-rollout-ga-prd\\n- Confluence design spec: hosted-canary-rollout-workflow-design-spec\\n- ADR: adr-hosted-rollout-cohorting-and-traffic-splitting\\n- ADR: adr-rollout-policy-evaluation-order-and-precedence\\n- Runbook: runbook-rollout-stuck-or-bad-split\\n- SLO/alerts: hosted-rollouts-slo-metrics-and-alerts\\n- Docs PR: redwood-docs PR-922\\n- Observability: observability-pack PR-184\",\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2025-02-24 (Paula Mendes): Drafted initial checklist structure. document.title: GA launch criteria + beta exit checklist — Hosted canary rollouts
document.content:
{
  "key": "PM-1859",
  "team": "product-management",
  "title": "GA launch criteria + beta exit checklist — Hosted canary rollouts",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P0",
  "created_at": "2025-02-20",
  "updated_at": "2025-03-22",
  "creator": "Paula Mendes",
  "assignee": "Marissa Cole",
  "project": "Hosted Canary Rollout Workflow (GA)",
  "cycle": "2025-W12",
  "estimate": "5",
  "due_date": "2025-04-04",
  "customer_impact": "high",
  "release": "console-2025.04",
  "security_review_required": "true",
  "labels": [
    "ga-readiness",
    "hosted",
    "rollouts",
    "console",
    "sre",
    "security",
    "docs",
    "support-enablement"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "PM-1843",
    "PM-1851",
    "ENG-9123",
    "ENG-9140",
    "ENG-9146",
    "ENG-9152",
    "ENG-9158",
    "ENG-9171",
    "ENG-9180",
    "DES-742",
    "DES-755",
    "DES-763"
  ],
  "sub_issues": [
    "Create GA go/no-go doc + signoff list (Console/Platform/SRE/Security/Support)",
    "Confirm default auto-stop thresholds by tier/region for GA",
    "Finalize customer-facing limitations/known issues section for docs",
    "Support macros + troubleshooting flow for auto-pause / split mismatch",
    "Run GA staging game day with stop/rollback + audit validation"
  ],
  "description": "Purpose
- Define the Beta Exit criteria and GA Launch checklist for the Hosted canary rollout workflow (percentage-based traffic splitting on Hosted routes).
- Align Console, Control Plane, Smart Routing/Data Plane, Telemetry/SRE, Security, Docs, and Support on what “GA-ready” means.
- Serve as the single checklist for the GA go/no-go meeting and as a record of what we validated.

Scope reminder (GA)
- Hosted routes only (Dedicated/Private: schema-compatible, not GA)
- Console wizard to create/run/pause/rollback, plus timeline/activity view and cohort comparison metrics
- Policy guardrails: max step size, min soak time, approval gates (RBAC), auto-stop/auto-rollback based on SLO metrics
- Audit logging + customer-visible activity timeline

Beta Exit Criteria (must meet before scheduling GA)
1) Design partner validation
- Minimum: 5 design partners enabled, with at least 3 running a real production canary on Hosted.
- At least 10 completed rollouts end-to-end (create → start → step changes → reach 100% OR rollback).
- No P0/P1 issues open related to incorrect routing split, inability to rollback, or audit trail gaps.
- Qualitative: partners confirm they can understand (a) current step, (b) what will happen next, (c) why auto-stop occurred, and (d) how to rollback.

2) Reliability outcomes during beta
- No unresolved incidents attributable to rollout feature causing widespread request misrouting or outages.
- Any beta incidents have documented root cause, fix merged, and backported as needed (e.g., metric timeout stall bugfix; split mismatch learnings).
- SRE signoff that alerts are actionable and not generating sustained alert storms.

3) Governance + safety outcomes during beta
- Policy guardrails enforced consistently across UI and API (no bypass via API for restricted actions).
- Approval gates tested with RBAC role(s) (rollout-approver) and common enterprise setups.
- Audit events present for all required action types, with correct actor identity and diffs.

GA Launch Checklist (go/no-go)
A) Functional completeness (Console + API)
Owner: Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin
- Wizard flow supports:
  - Selecting route, baseline model version/config, canary model version/config
  - Defining traffic schedule (step %, soak duration)
  - Configuring guardrails (max step size, min soak time) and showing validation errors clearly
  - Review + confirm with explicit warnings for destructive actions (rollback)
- Lifecycle actions supported and validated end-to-end:
  - Create rollout (draft)
  - Start rollout
  - Progress to next step (with/without approval gate)
  - Pause/resume
  - Rollback (manual) and “rollback to baseline” semantics
  - Auto-pause / auto-rollback on SLO breach (with reason surfaced)
- State machine correctness:
  - No “stuck” states on metric evaluation timeouts; clear retry + user-facing error
  - Idempotent retries for control plane → data plane propagation
- API parity for core operations (documented): create, get status, list activity, approve step, pause/resume, rollback

Acceptance evidence
- E2E test suite passing in CI and nightly (ENG-9164)
- Staging manual walkthrough recorded (link in go/no-go notes)

B) Smart Routing enforcement correctness
Owner: Mina Haddad / Ravi Menon
- Deterministic cohorting implemented and documented (hash inputs + stickiness rules)
- Percentage split accuracy within tolerance per region (define tolerance below)
- Correct behavior for:
  - Multi-region traffic
  - Streaming requests
  - Retries (client and internal)
  - Fallback routing interactions (baseline vs canary; precedence per ADR)
- Kill switch behavior verified:
  - Tenant-level disable immediately forces 100% baseline
  - Global disable forces baseline and prevents new rollouts from starting

Split accuracy target (GA)
- For stable traffic volume, measured canary proportion should converge to target within ±2% absolute over a 15-minute window (per region), excluding low-volume routes.
- For low volume routes, UI must display “insufficient volume” guidance instead of implying precise percentages.

Acceptance evidence
- Staging smoke tests (perf-canary PR-147)
- Post-fix validation for beta split mismatch scenario (see incident thread: rollout-split-mismatch-us-east)

C) Telemetry, dashboards, and alerting
Owner: Sean Gallagher / Aisha Bello / Logan Wright
Required cohort signals (tagging + aggregation)
- Every request must be attributable to:
  - route
  - model version/config (baseline vs canary)
  - cohort (baseline/canary)
  - region
  - rollout_id (with cardinality controls; ensure no blowups)
- Metrics required in Console comparison view + internal dashboards:
  - Request rate (RPS)
  - Error rate (overall, 5xx, timeouts)
  - Latency (p50/p95; ideally p99 in internal)
  - Tokens/sec and cost proxies (where available)
  - Streaming-specific failure modes (disconnects, partial completions) if tracked

Stop conditions (GA defaults)
- Auto-stop/auto-rollback must be available and enabled by default for new rollouts (with ability to tune thresholds by entitlement/tier).
- Default thresholds (initial GA proposal; finalize with SRE):
  - 5xx error rate: canary exceeds baseline by +1.0% absolute AND exceeds 2.0% absolute for 5 minutes
  - Timeout rate: canary exceeds baseline by +0.5% absolute for 5 minutes
  - p95 latency regression: canary p95 > baseline p95 * 1.25 for 10 minutes (guard for low volume)
- Rollout behavior on breach:
  - Auto-pause first if we can attribute breach confidently; auto-rollback when breach persists (or per policy)
  - Always emit: (1) customer-visible timeline entry, (2) audit event, (3) notification event

Alerting guidelines
- Alerts should page SRE only for:
  - Routing enforcement drift/incorrectness
  - Orchestrator stuck rollouts at scale
  - Global cohort tagging failures
  - Control plane → data plane propagation failures
- Customer route-specific canary SLO breaches should notify customer in Console/timeline and optionally via webhook/email (no paging unless systemic).

Acceptance evidence
- Cohort dashboards exist + validated against known traffic patterns (PR-28910 / observability pack PR-184)
- Cardinality analysis completed and within limits (Drive: rollout-cohort-metrics-cardinality-analysis)

D) Audit logging + change history (Security/Compliance)
Owner: Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei
Required audit event coverage
- Events must be emitted for:
  - rollout.created
  - rollout.started
  - rollout.step.approval_requested
  - rollout.step.approved / rollout.step.denied
  - rollout.step.changed (percent change)
  - rollout.paused / rollout.resumed
  - rollout.rolled_back (manual)
  - rollout.auto_paused / rollout.auto_rolled_back (include stop condition + metric snapshot reference)
  - rollout.completed
- Required fields (high level): tenant_id, actor_id/actor_type, route_id, rollout_id, previous_state → new_state, diff (human readable + structured), timestamp, request_id/trace_id when applicable.
- Retention and export:
  - Align with existing audit log retention policy by tier
  - Verify SIEM export compatibility (field naming and size limits)

Customer-visible activity timeline
- Must match audit events but may exclude security-only internal fields; should show “what happened” and “why” (e.g., auto-pause reason).

Acceptance evidence
- Security review of audit event schema doc (Confluence: audit-events-rollout-actions)
- Sample events captured in staging and validated by Security (screenshots/log dumps referenced in go/no-go)

E) Policy guardrails + RBAC
Owner: Jordan Lee / Kaitlyn Nguyen
- Guardrails enforced for step changes:
  - Max step size (e.g., 1% → 50% disallowed without override/approval)
  - Minimum soak time before next step
  - Approval gates configurable by tenant/admin policy
- Entitlement mapping documented:
  - Which customers get auto-rollback, approvals, advanced retention, etc.
- RBAC roles validated:
  - Who can create rollouts
  - Who can start/pause/rollback
  - Who can approve (rollout-approver role)
- UI error messaging must reflect policy engine errors with actionable guidance (e.g., “Wait 20m more to satisfy min soak”)

Acceptance evidence
- Policy engine tests and Console integration tests pass (PR-28802)
- Manual validation with at least 2 common enterprise role setups

F) Documentation (public + internal)
Owner: Elliot Price / Wei Chen
Customer docs must include
- Conceptual overview: baseline vs canary, cohorting, step schedule, soak time
- Step-by-step Console walkthrough
- API reference (or links) for rollout operations
- Troubleshooting:
  - Why a rollout auto-paused
  - Why metrics show “insufficient volume”
  - Split mismatch debugging steps (what to check before contacting support)
  - How to rollback safely
- Limitations (GA):
  - No bandits/dynamic optimization
  - Quality gates optional/manual (not hard gates)
  - Dedicated/Private not GA

Internal docs must include
- Enablement how-to (feature flags, permissions, sanity checks)
- On-call runbook for stuck rollout / bad split
- Release/change management checklist

Acceptance evidence
- Docs PR merged (redwood-docs PR-922)
- Runbooks published (Confluence) and reviewed with SRE + Support

G) Support readiness + incident response
Owner: Dev Patel / Rafael Mendes
- Support playbooks:
  - Triage flow for “rollout paused unexpectedly after latency spike”
  - Triage flow for “traffic split not matching config”
  - Escalation path to on-call / engineering
  - What data to request: tenant_id, route, rollout_id, timeframe, region, request IDs
- Macros/snippets created for common questions (e.g., “How do I do a percentage rollout on Hosted route?”)
- SLA for response during GA launch week and ownership for escalation channel

Acceptance evidence
- At least 2 support training sessions run (recording link in go/no-go)
- Sample tickets resolved using new macros (reference: SUP-48211, SUP-48302, SUP-48377)

H) Release management + staged rollout plan
Owner: Connor O'Brien / Soojin Lee
- Feature flags:
  - Per-tenant enablement
  - Internal dogfood tenants first
  - Staged cohort of beta → expanded beta → GA default (if applicable)
  - Kill switch playbook (owners + steps)
- Migration/backward compatibility validated for config schema changes
- Backout strategy:
  - Disable canary UI
  - Force baseline routing
  - Preserve audit logs and rollout history for completed rollouts

Acceptance evidence
- Change management checklist completed (Drive: hosted-canary-ga-change-management-checklist)
- Release readiness review held 48–72 hours pre-GA

Go/No-Go Process (how we decide)
Meeting: GA Readiness Review (60 minutes)
Required attendees / signoffs
- Product: Marissa Cole (final call)
- Console Eng: Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin
- Platform/Policy: Ethan Park / Jordan Lee
- Smart Routing: Mina Haddad
- SRE: Sean Gallagher or Rafael Mendes
- Security: Marcus Lin
- Docs/Support: Elliot Price + Dev Patel

Decision rules
- No-go if any of:
  - Known issue causing incorrect split enforcement at material rates
  - Rollback unavailable or unreliable
  - Missing audit events for any action type listed above
  - Unbounded metrics cardinality risk unresolved
  - No validated kill switch
- Conditional go allowed if:
  - Minor UI polish issues only
  - Non-blocking docs follow-ups with explicit owner + date
  - Non-paging alert tuning improvements queued (does not impact safety)

Artifacts to attach in go/no-go notes
- Links: PRD, design spec, ADRs
- Latest beta partner tracker snapshot
- List of open bugs (P0/P1 only) with owners + ETA
- Staging game day results + any follow-ups

Current status / open questions (as of last update)
- Need final agreement on GA default thresholds by region/tier; beta feedback suggests p95 multiplier threshold may be too aggressive for long-context routes.
- Confirm whether GA requires customer notifications beyond Console timeline (e.g., webhook). If not in GA, docs must state Console-only.
- Ensure “insufficient volume” guidance text matches design copy and does not confuse customers about split accuracy.

Links
- Confluence PRD: hosted-canary-rollout-ga-prd
- Confluence design spec: hosted-canary-rollout-workflow-design-spec
- ADR: adr-hosted-rollout-cohorting-and-traffic-splitting
- ADR: adr-rollout-policy-evaluation-order-and-precedence
- Runbook: runbook-rollout-stuck-or-bad-split
- SLO/alerts: hosted-rollouts-slo-metrics-and-alerts
- Docs PR: redwood-docs PR-922
- Observability: observability-pack PR-184",

    "title": "How do I do a percentage-based canary rollout on a Hosted route?",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/jira",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"SUP-48211\",\n  \"project\": \"customer-support\",\n  \"issue_type\": \"Question\",\n  \"summary\": \"How do I do a percentage-based canary rollout on a Hosted route?\",\n  \"status\": \"Closed\",\n  \"priority\": \"P3\",\n  \"severity\": \"Sev3\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-03-21\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2025-03-24\",\n  \"reporter\": \"Dev Patel\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Owen Phillips\",\n  \"customer_company\": \"Northstar Support AI\",\n  \"customer_tier\": \"enterprise\",\n  \"components\": [\n    \"console\",\n    \"platform-control-plane\",\n    \"smart-routing\",\n    \"telemetry\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"hosted\",\n    \"rollouts\",\n    \"canary\",\n    \"traffic-splitting\",\n    \"how-to\",\n    \"beta\"\n  ],\n  \"environment\": \"prod (us-east)\",\n  \"affected_regions\": [\n    \"us-east\"\n  ],\n  \"first_response_due_at\": \"2025-03-22\",\n  \"sla_due_at\": \"2025-03-26\",\n  \"linked_issues\": [\n    \"SUP-48302\",\n    \"SUP-48377\"\n  ],\n  \"related_github_prs\": [\n    \"sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-922-console-hosted-canary-rollouts-ga-docs.json\"\n  ],\n  \"related_confluence_pages\": [\n    \"sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/hosted-canary-rollout-workflow-design-spec.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/hosted-canary-rollout-ga-prd.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-platform/how-tos/how-to-enable-hosted-canary-rollouts-for-a-tenant.json\"\n  ],\n  \"description\": \"Customer question (via support portal):\\n\\n\\\"We currently have a Hosted route pinned to a model version. We want to try a new model version/config but only send ~1\\u20135% of traffic at first and then ramp up. What\\u2019s the recommended way to do a percent-based rollout in Redwood? Is this available in Console and/or API?\\\"\\n\\nRequested outcomes:\\n- Step-by-step instructions for percentage-based traffic splitting on a Hosted route\\n- Clarify beta vs GA availability and enablement requirements\\n- Links to docs / troubleshooting notes\\n\\nImpact:\\n- No current outage; customer is blocked on safe introduction of a new model version.\\n\\nNotes:\\n- Customer mentioned they want cohort stickiness per end-user/session if possible (avoid one user seeing mixed behavior during rollout).\\n- They also asked about auto-rollback if latency spikes.\\n\\nSupport owner: Owen Phillips\\nSupport readiness contact: Dev Patel\",\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2025-03-21 (Dev Patel): Acknowledged. Confirming: (1) you\\u2019re using a Hosted route (not Dedicated/Private), and (2) you want a controlled traffic split between baseline and canary model versions. Also: do you need approval gates (separation of duties) and auto-pause/rollback on SLO breach?\",\n    \"2025-03-21 (Customer - Northstar Support AI): Yes, Hosted route. We\\u2019d like the ability to ramp 1%\\u21925%\\u219225%\\u219250%\\u2192100% with a minimum soak time per step. Ideally approval gates for production. Auto-rollback on high error/latency would be great. We primarily use Console but can automate via API later.\",\n    \"2025-03-21 (Owen Phillips): Guidance + current availability:\\n\\n1) Availability (beta vs GA)\\n- Percentage-based canary rollouts for Hosted routes are currently in limited beta for select tenants.\\n- If your tenant is not enabled yet, we can request enablement; once enabled, you will see a new \\u201cRollouts\\u201d section on the Hosted route page in Console.\\n- GA is in progress; functionality and schema will remain compatible, but UI wording and guardrail defaults may tighten at GA.\\n\\n2) Console workflow (recommended)\\n- Go to Console \\u2192 Hosted \\u2192 Routes \\u2192 select the route you want to change.\\n- Open the \\u201cRollouts\\u201d tab \\u2192 \\u201cCreate canary rollout\\u201d.\\n- Choose:\\n  a) Baseline: current model version/config (what\\u2019s serving today)\\n  b) Canary: new model version/config\\n- Define the traffic schedule (example): 1% \\u2192 5% \\u2192 25% \\u2192 50% \\u2192 100%.\\n- Set minimum soak time per step (e.g., 20\\u201330 minutes during business hours; longer for lower-traffic routes).\\n- Guardrails / stop conditions (recommended defaults):\\n  - Auto-pause or auto-rollback if canary cohort breaches thresholds on 5xx/timeouts and p95 latency regression vs baseline.\\n  - Optionally require approval to advance steps (requires rollout approver permission).\\n- Review & confirm to create the rollout. Start it when ready.\\n\\n3) Monitoring baseline vs canary\\n- While the rollout is running, use the \\u201cMetrics comparison\\u201d view to compare baseline vs canary cohorts for:\\n  - Error rate (5xx)\\n  - Timeout rate\\n  - Latency (p50/p95)\\n  - Throughput / tokens per second (where available)\\n- The rollout timeline view will show step changes, approvals, pauses, and any auto-stop events.\\n\\n4) Rollback / pause\\n- You can pause at any step (keeps split stable) and either resume later or rollback.\\n- Rollback sets traffic back to baseline immediately and records an activity/audit entry.\\n\\n5) Cohort stickiness\\n- The rollout splitter is deterministic; to keep an end-user consistently in baseline vs canary, pass a stable key per user/session in your requests.\\n- If you share your integration details (SDK + what identifiers you can provide), we can recommend the best header/field to use for consistent cohorting.\\n\\nDocs (customer-facing):\\n- https://docs.redwoodinference.com/console/rollouts/hosted-canary\\n- https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/safe-rollouts\\n\\nIf you want, reply with your Redwood org/tenant ID and the route name, and we\\u2019ll confirm whether the beta flag is already enabled for you.\",\n    \"2025-03-22 (Customer - Northstar Support AI): Thanks. We don\\u2019t see the Rollouts tab yet. Tenant ID: nsai-prod-117. Route: support-agent-prod. We also want approval gates (our ops team approves prod changes).\",\n    \"2025-03-22 (Dev Patel): Internal: requesting enablement for tenant nsai-prod-117. Also confirming whether \\u201crollout-approver\\u201d role is enabled for their org. Looping in release/change management to make sure the kill switch is documented for this tenant.\",\n    \"2025-03-22 (Owen Phillips): Confirmed you\\u2019re not enabled yet. We\\u2019ve put in an enablement request for nsai-prod-117.\\n\\nOn approvals: once enabled, you can configure the rollout to require approval to advance steps (e.g., after 1% soak completes, it will wait for an approver to advance to 5%). We can also help you map the correct Console roles so only your ops team can approve.\\n\\nETA: typically same business day for beta enablement; we\\u2019ll update here once complete.\",\n    \"2025-03-23 (Owen Phillips): Enablement complete for nsai-prod-117. Please refresh Console and check Hosted \\u2192 Routes \\u2192 support-agent-prod \\u2192 Rollouts.\\n\\nRBAC notes:\\n- To create/start rollouts: Route Admin (or equivalent)\\n- To approve step changes when approval gates are enabled: Rollout Approver\\n\\nIf you share the emails of the users who should have the approver role (or your IdP group name if using SSO), we can help validate the mapping.\",\n    \"2025-03-24 (Customer - Northstar Support AI): We see it now. We created a rollout and can set the step schedule + soak time and approvals. This is exactly what we needed. We\\u2019ll follow the docs for cohort stickiness. Thanks!\"\n  ],\n  \"resolution\": \"Provided step-by-step guidance for percentage-based Hosted canary rollouts in Console, clarified beta vs GA availability, and enabled the feature flag for tenant nsai-prod-117. Shared customer-facing docs links and RBAC requirements for approval gates. Customer confirmed successful setup and closed the request.\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"summary\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"comments\",\n    \"resolution\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_c67a7f60aa1b4f3c81e82921aa73610a\"\n}",
