document.title: How do I do a percentage-based canary rollout on a Hosted route?
document.content:
{
  "key": "SUP-48211",
  "project": "customer-support",
  "issue_type": "Question",
  "summary": "How do I do a percentage-based canary rollout on a Hosted route?",
  "status": "Closed",
  "priority": "P3",
  "severity": "Sev3",
  "created_at": "2025-03-21",
  "updated_at": "2025-03-24",
  "reporter": "Dev Patel",
  "assignee": "Owen Phillips",
  "customer_company": "Northstar Support AI",
  "customer_tier": "enterprise",
  "components": [
    "console",
    "platform-control-plane",
    "smart-routing",
    "telemetry"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "hosted",
    "rollouts",
    "canary",
    "traffic-splitting",
    "how-to",
    "beta"
  ],
  "environment": "prod (us-east)",
  "affected_regions": [
    "us-east"
  ],
  "first_response_due_at": "2025-03-22",
  "sla_due_at": "2025-03-26",
  "linked_issues": [
    "SUP-48302",
    "SUP-48377"
  ],
  "related_github_prs": [
    "sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-922-console-hosted-canary-rollouts-ga-docs.json"
  ],
  "related_confluence_pages": [
    "sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/hosted-canary-rollout-workflow-design-spec.json",
    "sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/hosted-canary-rollout-ga-prd.json",
    "sources/confluence/eng-platform/how-tos/how-to-enable-hosted-canary-rollouts-for-a-tenant.json"
  ],
  "description": "Customer question (via support portal):

"We currently have a Hosted route pinned to a model version. We want to try a new model version/config but only send ~1–5% of traffic at first and then ramp up. What’s the recommended way to do a percent-based rollout in Redwood? Is this available in Console and/or API?"

Requested outcomes:
- Step-by-step instructions for percentage-based traffic splitting on a Hosted route
- Clarify beta vs GA availability and enablement requirements
- Links to docs / troubleshooting notes

Impact:
- No current outage; customer is blocked on safe introduction of a new model version.

Notes:
- Customer mentioned they want cohort stickiness per end-user/session if possible (avoid one user seeing mixed behavior during rollout).
- They also asked about auto-rollback if latency spikes.

Support owner: Owen Phillips
Support readiness contact: Dev Patel",
  "comments": [
    "2025-03-21 (Dev Patel): Acknowledged. Confirming: (1) you’re using a Hosted route (not Dedicated/Private), and (2) you want a controlled traffic split between baseline and canary model versions. Also: do you need approval gates (separation of duties) and auto-pause/rollback on SLO breach?",
    "2025-03-21 (Customer - Northstar Support AI): Yes, Hosted route. We’d like the ability to ramp 1%→5%→25%→50%→100% with a minimum soak time per step. Ideally approval gates for production. Auto-rollback on high error/latency would be great. We primarily use Console but can automate via API later.",
    "2025-03-21 (Owen Phillips): Guidance + current availability:

1) Availability (beta vs GA)
- Percentage-based canary rollouts for Hosted routes are currently in limited beta for select tenants.
- If your tenant is not enabled yet, we can request enablement; once enabled, you will see a new “Rollouts” section on the Hosted route page in Console.
- GA is in progress; functionality and schema will remain compatible, but UI wording and guardrail defaults may tighten at GA.

2) Console workflow (recommended)
- Go to Console → Hosted → Routes → select the route you want to change.
- Open the “Rollouts” tab → “Create canary rollout”.
- Choose:
  a) Baseline: current model version/config (what’s serving today)
  b) Canary: new model version/config
- Define the traffic schedule (example): 1% → 5% → 25% → 50% → 100%.
- Set minimum soak time per step (e.g., 20–30 minutes during business hours; longer for lower-traffic routes).
- Guardrails / stop conditions (recommended defaults):
  - Auto-pause or auto-rollback if canary cohort breaches thresholds on 5xx/timeouts and p95 latency regression vs baseline.
  - Optionally require approval to advance steps (requires rollout approver permission).
- Review & confirm to create the rollout. Start it when ready.

3) Monitoring baseline vs canary
- While the rollout is running, use the “Metrics comparison” view to compare baseline vs canary cohorts for:
  - Error rate (5xx)
  - Timeout rate
  - Latency (p50/p95)
  - Throughput / tokens per second (where available)
- The rollout timeline view will show step changes, approvals, pauses, and any auto-stop events.

4) Rollback / pause
- You can pause at any step (keeps split stable) and either resume later or rollback.
- Rollback sets traffic back to baseline immediately and records an activity/audit entry.

5) Cohort stickiness
- The rollout splitter is deterministic; to keep an end-user consistently in baseline vs canary, pass a stable key per user/session in your requests.
- If you share your integration details (SDK + what identifiers you can provide), we can recommend the best header/field to use for consistent cohorting.

Docs (customer-facing):
- https://docs.redwoodinference.com/console/rollouts/hosted-canary
- https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/safe-rollouts

If you want, reply with your Redwood org/tenant ID and the route name, and we’ll confirm whether the beta flag is already enabled for you.",
    "2025-03-22 (Customer - Northstar Support AI): Thanks. We don’t see the Rollouts tab yet. Tenant ID: nsai-prod-117. Route: support-agent-prod. We also want approval gates (our ops team approves prod changes).",
    "2025-03-22 (Dev Patel): Internal: requesting enablement for tenant nsai-prod-117. Also confirming whether “rollout-approver” role is enabled for their org. Looping in release/change management to make sure the kill switch is documented for this tenant.",
    "2025-03-22 (Owen Phillips): Confirmed you’re not enabled yet. We’ve put in an enablement request for nsai-prod-117.

On approvals: once enabled, you can configure the rollout to require approval to advance steps (e.g., after 1% soak completes, it will wait for an approver to advance to 5%). We can also help you map the correct Console roles so only your ops team can approve.

ETA: typically same business day for beta enablement; we’ll update here once complete.",
    "2025-03-23 (Owen Phillips): Enablement complete for nsai-prod-117. Please refresh Console and check Hosted → Routes → support-agent-prod → Rollouts.

RBAC notes:
- To create/start rollouts: Route Admin (or equivalent)
- To approve step changes when approval gates are enabled: Rollout Approver

If you share the emails of the users who should have the approver role (or your IdP group name if using SSO), we can help validate the mapping.",
    "2025-03-24 (Customer - Northstar Support AI): We see it now. We created a rollout and can set the step schedule + soak time and approvals. This is exactly what we needed. We’ll follow the docs for cohort stickiness. Thanks!"
  ],
  "resolution": "Provided step-by-step guidance for percentage-based Hosted canary rollouts in Console, clarified beta vs GA availability, and enabled the feature flag for tenant nsai-prod-117. Shared customer-facing docs links and RBAC requirements for approval gates. Customer confirmed successful setup and closed the request.",
  "title_field_name": "summary",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "comments",
    "resolution"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_c67a7f60aa1b4f3c81e82921aa73610a"
}

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/jira",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"SUP-48302\",\n  \"project\": \"customer-support\",\n  \"issue_type\": \"Bug\",\n  \"summary\": \"Hosted canary rollout auto-paused unexpectedly after brief p95 latency spike (beta customer)\",\n  \"status\": \"Resolved\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"severity\": \"Sev2\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-03-27\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2025-04-02\",\n  \"reporter\": \"Dev Patel\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Owen Phillips\",\n  \"customer_company\": \"Northstar Support AI\",\n  \"customer_tier\": \"enterprise\",\n  \"components\": [\n    \"console\",\n    \"telemetry\",\n    \"rollout-orchestrator\",\n    \"smart-routing\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"hosted-canary\",\n    \"beta\",\n    \"auto-stop\",\n    \"latency\",\n    \"slo-thresholds\",\n    \"needs-threshold-tuning\"\n  ],\n  \"environment\": \"prod/us-east\",\n  \"affected_models\": [\n    \"rw-mistral-7b-instruct-v3 (baseline)\",\n    \"rw-mistral-7b-instruct-v3-canary-q8 (canary)\"\n  ],\n  \"affected_regions\": [\n    \"us-east\"\n  ],\n  \"first_response_due_at\": \"2025-03-27\",\n  \"sla_due_at\": \"2025-03-28\",\n  \"linked_issues\": [\n    \"SUP-48377\"\n  ],\n  \"related_incident_id\": \"INC-2025-03-27-us-east-gateway-latency\",\n  \"related_github_prs\": [\n    \"redwood/pr-28845-auto-stop-rollback-on-slo-breach\",\n    \"redwood/pr-28910-add-rollout-cohort-dashboards-and-alert-templates\"\n  ],\n  \"related_confluence_pages\": [\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/hosted-rollouts-slo-metrics-and-alerts.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/runbook-rollout-stuck-or-bad-split.json\"\n  ],\n  \"description\": \"Customer reports their Hosted canary rollout auto-paused at the 25% step immediately after a short latency spike, despite overall application health appearing normal. They want to understand why it paused, whether this indicates a canary regression, and how to tune/avoid false positives during beta.\\n\\nIssue summary\\n- What: Rollout transitioned to AUTO_PAUSED with reason \\\"p95 latency regression > threshold\\\".\\n- When: 2025-03-27 ~18:10\\u201318:25 UTC during step 25%.\\n- Where: prod/us-east, route: /v1/chat/completions (Northstar customer route alias: support-agent-prod).\\n- Impact: Rollout progression blocked; customer held at 25% canary traffic for ~45 minutes until manual action. No hard outage, but rollout confidence reduced.\\n\\nCustomer-reported symptoms\\n- Console showed: \\\"Rollout paused automatically due to SLO breach\\\".\\n- Customer observed: brief latency increase across their app; no material increase in 5xx; canary model did not appear uniquely affected.\\n\\nExpected behavior\\n- Auto-pause/rollback should trigger when canary cohort is reliably worse than baseline beyond configured thresholds, not when both baseline and canary are affected by a transient regional issue.\\n\\nActual behavior\\n- Auto-pause triggered on a short p95 spike; cohort comparison logic flagged canary regression even though baseline p95 also spiked in the same window.\\n\\nInitial hypothesis\\n- Threshold sensitivity + evaluation window too short at 25% traffic created a false positive under transient regional latency. Also possible that the comparison job sampled unevenly across cohorts during the spike.\\n\\nNotes\\n- This ticket is part of Hosted canary rollouts beta feedback. Customer asked for recommended settings (min soak time / evaluation window / sample size) and whether thresholds are configurable per route.\\n\",\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2025-03-27 18:33 UTC \\u2014 Dev Patel (Support): Ticket created from customer email + #support escalation. Asking SRE to validate whether this was a real canary regression or a regional event. Customer asking for explanation + recommended tuning.\",\n    \"2025-03-27 18:41 UTC \\u2014 Owen Phillips (Support, assignee): Acknowledged. Pulling rollout timeline + cohort dashboards. Requested customer provide rollout_id and approximate timestamps + route name (if multiple).\",\n    \"2025-03-27 18:49 UTC \\u2014 Customer (Northstar Support AI): Rollout ID rlt_7Qm2... Route: support-agent-prod. Step schedule was 1% (30m) \\u2192 5% (30m) \\u2192 25% (60m). Auto-paused ~10 min after entering 25%. We didn\\u2019t see error rate changes; did see increased latency for all requests for a bit. Can you confirm if canary is actually worse? We want to finish rollout today if safe.\",\n    \"2025-03-27 19:05 UTC \\u2014 Aisha Bello (SRE): Checked cohort dashboard template (rollout_id=rlt_7Qm2...) in us-east. Observed p95 spike in both baseline and canary around 18:12\\u201318:18 UTC. Canary p95 looked slightly higher but sample size small while traffic was ramping (recent step change). Also correlates with gateway latency incident in us-east (INC-2025-03-27-us-east-gateway-latency).\",\n    \"2025-03-27 19:12 UTC \\u2014 Owen Phillips (Support): Confirmed: event reason is \\\"p95 latency regression\\\" with threshold 20% relative vs baseline over a 5-minute lookback. Triggered at 18:16 UTC. Not seeing canary-only error rate changes. Likely false-positive due to transient regional latency + short lookback during step transition.\\n\\nAction: recommending customer resume rollout after us-east incident cleared, with temporarily relaxed stop condition or longer evaluation window for the 25% step.\",\n    \"2025-03-27 19:18 UTC \\u2014 Sean Gallagher (SRE lead): Agree false positive. For beta, default p95 regression threshold + short window is aggressive at early traffic volumes. Recommend tuning: (1) add minimum sample size gating before evaluating p95 regression; (2) increase evaluation window to 10\\u201315m; (3) add a 3\\u20135m grace period after step changes. Logging follow-up for product/eng; this will reduce churn in beta.\",\n    \"2025-03-27 19:26 UTC \\u2014 Owen Phillips (Support) to Customer: Root cause appears to be a brief us-east platform latency event impacting BOTH baseline and canary. The auto-pause was triggered by our default rule (p95 regression >20% over 5m) during a step transition (low/uneven samples). We do not currently see evidence the canary model is uniquely worse.\\n\\nRecommendation: Resume rollout once p95 stabilizes (we\\u2019re seeing it back to normal now). For this rollout, either (a) temporarily disable p95-based auto-pause for the next step, or (b) widen lookback to 15m and increase threshold to 35% for the remainder of today. We can help apply settings in Console.\",\n    \"2025-03-27 19:44 UTC \\u2014 Customer (Northstar Support AI): Thanks. We resumed at 25% and it has been stable for ~20m. Please share recommended defaults for next rollouts; we want guardrails but fewer false pauses.\",\n    \"2025-03-27 20:10 UTC \\u2014 Owen Phillips (Support): Shared beta guidance: for chat workloads with bursty traffic, use min soak 30\\u201360m and 10\\u201315m evaluation windows; add min sample size (we suggest >=2k requests per cohort) before enabling p95 regression gating; keep 5xx/timeout stop conditions enabled at tighter thresholds.\\n\\nAlso: This aligns with internal SRE guidance page on Hosted rollout SLO metrics/alerts (linked).\",\n    \"2025-03-28 16:02 UTC \\u2014 Dev Patel (Support): Internal note: filing feedback to product/eng to adjust beta defaults (sample-size gating + grace after step changes). Linking incident so this doesn\\u2019t get mistaken for model regression.\",\n    \"2025-04-01 17:31 UTC \\u2014 Jordan Lee (Policy Engine): FYI we can enforce safer defaults via policy for beta tenants (min soak + max sensitivity). However, current UX still allows aggressive latency rule with short lookback. Suggest we update recommended preset in wizard and add warning copy when lookback <10m at <50% traffic.\",\n    \"2025-04-02 09:08 UTC \\u2014 Owen Phillips (Support): Customer confirmed rollout completed (100%) on 2025-03-28 with no further auto-pauses. Closing as resolved. Follow-up action tracked with product/eng separately (beta defaults + grace period + sample size gating).\"\n  ],\n  \"resolution\": \"Determined auto-pause was a false positive triggered by default p95 latency regression rule during a transient us-east latency incident affecting both cohorts, combined with a short evaluation window and low/uneven sample sizes immediately after a step change. Customer resumed rollout after the event cleared and completed rollout successfully.\\n\\nCustomer-facing outcome\\n- Provided explanation with timestamps + cohort dashboard interpretation.\\n- Recommended threshold tuning (longer lookback, higher regression threshold temporarily, minimum sample-size gating) for subsequent rollouts.\\n\\nInternal outcome\\n- Captured beta feedback to adjust recommended wizard defaults and to add safeguards (sample size + grace period after step transitions) to reduce false pauses.\",\n  \"next_steps\": [\n    \"Product/Eng: Update rollout wizard recommended preset for latency stop conditions (lookback >=10m; guidance when <50% traffic).\",\n    \"SRE/Telemetry: Add minimum sample-size gating for p95 regression evaluation and a grace period after step changes (beta hardening).\",\n    \"Support: Add this scenario to canned responses / troubleshooting for \\\"rollout paused unexpectedly\\\" with links to cohort dashboards and the runbook.\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"summary\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"comments\",\n    \"resolution\",\n    \"next_steps\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_dcdece5c12124b378e480e5c0d987a76\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted canary rollout auto-paused unexpectedly after brief p95 latency spike (beta customer)\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/jira\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-48302-rollout-paused-unexpectedly-after-latency-spike.json\nConnector: jira\nWorkspace: customer-support\nProject: customer-support\n\nat 25 % canary traffic for ~ 45 minutes until manual action. no hard outage, but rollout confidence reduced. customer - reported symptoms - console showed : \" rollout paused automatically due to slo breach \". - customer observed : brief latency increase across their app ; no material increase in 5xx ; canary model did not appear uniquely affected. expected behavior - auto - pause / rollback should trigger when canary cohort is reliably worse than baseline beyond configured thresholds, not when both baseline and canary are affected by a transient regional issue. actual behavior - auto - pause triggered on a short p95 spike ; cohort comparison logic flagged canary regression even though baseline p95 also spiked in the same window.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted canary rollout auto-paused unexpectedly after brief p95 latency spike (beta customer)\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/jira\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-48302-rollout-paused-unexpectedly-after-latency-spike.json\nConnector: jira\nWorkspace: customer-support\nProject: customer-support\n\nresolution : determined auto - pause was a false positive triggered by default p95 latency regression rule during a transient us - east latency incident affecting both cohorts, combined with a short evaluation window and low / uneven sample sizes immediately after a step change. customer resumed rollout after the event cleared and completed rollout successfully. customer - facing outcome - provided explanation with timestamps + cohort dashboard interpretation. - recommended threshold tuning ( longer lookback, higher regression threshold temporarily, minimum sample - size gating ) for subsequent rollouts. internal outcome - captured beta feedback to adjust recommended wizard defaults and to add safeguards ( sample size + grace period after step transitions ) to reduce false pauses. # # next steps",

document.title: Hosted canary rollout auto-paused unexpectedly after brief p95 latency spike (beta customer)
document.content:
{
  "key": "SUP-48302",
  "project": "customer-support",
  "issue_type": "Bug",
  "summary": "Hosted canary rollout auto-paused unexpectedly after brief p95 latency spike (beta customer)",
  "status": "Resolved",
  "priority": "P1",
  "severity": "Sev2",
  "created_at": "2025-03-27",
  "updated_at": "2025-04-02",
  "reporter": "Dev Patel",
  "assignee": "Owen Phillips",
  "customer_company": "Northstar Support AI",
  "customer_tier": "enterprise",
  "components": [
    "console",
    "telemetry",
    "rollout-orchestrator",
    "smart-routing"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "hosted-canary",
    "beta",
    "auto-stop",
    "latency",
    "slo-thresholds",
    "needs-threshold-tuning"
  ],
  "environment": "prod/us-east",
  "affected_models": [
    "rw-mistral-7b-instruct-v3 (baseline)",
    "rw-mistral-7b-instruct-v3-canary-q8 (canary)"
  ],
  "affected_regions": [
    "us-east"
  ],
  "first_response_due_at": "2025-03-27",
  "sla_due_at": "2025-03-28",
  "linked_issues": [
    "SUP-48377"
  ],
  "related_incident_id": "INC-2025-03-27-us-east-gateway-latency",
  "related_github_prs": [
    "redwood/pr-28845-auto-stop-rollback-on-slo-breach",
    "redwood/pr-28910-add-rollout-cohort-dashboards-and-alert-templates"
  ],
  "related_confluence_pages": [
    "sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/hosted-rollouts-slo-metrics-and-alerts.json",
    "sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/runbook-rollout-stuck-or-bad-split.json"
  ],
  "description": "Customer reports their Hosted canary rollout auto-paused at the 25% step immediately after a short latency spike, despite overall application health appearing normal. They want to understand why it paused, whether this indicates a canary regression, and how to tune/avoid false positives during beta.\n\nIssue summary\n- What: Rollout transitioned to AUTO_PAUSED with reason \"p95 latency regression > threshold\".\n- When: 2025-03-27 ~18:10\u201318:25 UTC during step 25%.\n- Where: prod/us-east, route: /v1/chat/completions (Northstar customer route alias: support-agent-prod).\n- Impact: Rollout progression blocked; customer held at 25% canary traffic for ~45 minutes until manual action. No hard outage, but rollout confidence reduced.\n\nCustomer-reported symptoms\n- Console showed: \"Rollout paused automatically due to SLO breach\".\n- Customer observed: brief latency increase across their app; no material increase in 5xx; canary model did not appear uniquely affected.\n\nExpected behavior\n- Auto-pause/rollback should trigger when canary cohort is reliably worse than baseline beyond configured thresholds, not when both baseline and canary are affected by a transient regional issue.\n\nActual behavior\n- Auto-pause triggered on a short p95 spike; cohort comparison logic flagged canary regression even though baseline p95 also spiked in the same window.\n\nInitial hypothesis\n- Threshold sensitivity + evaluation window too short at 25% traffic created a false positive under transient regional latency. Also possible that the comparison job sampled unevenly across cohorts during the spike.\n\nNotes\n- This ticket is part of Hosted canary rollouts beta feedback. Customer asked for recommended settings (min soak time / evaluation window / sample size) and whether thresholds are configurable per route.\n",
  "comments": [
    "2025-03-27 18:33 UTC \u2014 Dev Patel (Support): Ticket created from customer email + #support escalation. Asking SRE to validate whether this was a real canary regression or a regional event. Customer asking for explanation + recommended tuning.",
    "2025-03-27 18:41 UTC \u2014 Owen Phillips (Support, assignee): Acknowledged. Pulling rollout timeline + cohort dashboards. Requested customer provide rollout_id and approximate timestamps + route name (if multiple).",
    "2025-03-27 18:49 UTC \u2014 Customer (Northstar Support AI): Rollout ID rlt_7Qm2... Route: support-agent-prod. Step schedule was 1% (30m) \u2192 5% (30m) \u2192 25% (60m). Auto-paused ~10 min after entering 25%. We didn\u2019t see error rate changes; did see increased latency for all requests for a bit. Can you confirm if canary is actually worse? We want to finish rollout today if safe.",
    "2025-03-27 19:05 UTC \u2014 Aisha Bello (SRE): Checked cohort dashboard template (rollout_id=rlt_7Qm2...) in us-east. Observed p95 spike in both baseline and canary around 18:12\u201318:18 UTC. Canary p95 looked slightly higher but sample size small while traffic was ramping (recent step change). Also correlates with gateway latency incident in us-east (INC-2025-03-27-us-east-gateway-latency).",
    "2025-03-27 19:12 UTC \u2014 Owen Phillips (Support): Confirmed: event reason is \"p95 latency regression\" with threshold 20% relative vs baseline over a 5-minute lookback. Triggered at 18:16 UTC. Not seeing canary-only error rate changes. Likely false-positive due to transient regional latency + short lookback during step transition.\n\nAction: recommending customer resume rollout after us-east incident cleared, with temporarily relaxed stop condition or longer evaluation window for the 25% step.",
    "2025-03-27 19:18 UTC \u2014 Sean Gallagher (SRE lead): Agree false positive. For beta, default p95 regression threshold + short window is aggressive at early traffic volumes. Recommend tuning: (1) add minimum sample size gating before evaluating p95 regression; (2) increase evaluation window to 10\u201315m; (3) add a 3\u20135m grace period after step changes. Logging follow-up for product/eng; this will reduce churn in beta.",
    "2025-03-27 19:26 UTC \u2014 Owen Phillips (Support) to Customer: Root cause appears to be a brief us-east platform latency event impacting BOTH baseline and canary. The auto-pause was triggered by our default rule (p95 regression >20% over 5m) during a step transition (low/uneven samples). We do not currently see evidence the canary model is uniquely worse.\n\nRecommendation: Resume rollout once p95 stabilizes (we\u2019re seeing it back to normal now). For this rollout, either (a) temporarily disable p95-based auto-pause for the next step, or (b) widen lookback to 15m and increase threshold to 35% for the remainder of today. We can help apply settings in Console.",
    "2025-03-27 19:44 UTC \u2014 Customer (Northstar Support AI): Thanks. We resumed at 25% and it has been stable for ~20m. Please share recommended defaults for next rollouts; we want guardrails but fewer false pauses.",
    "2025-03-27 20:10 UTC \u2014 Owen Phillips (Support): Shared beta guidance: for chat workloads with bursty traffic, use min soak 30\u201360m and 10\u201315m evaluation windows; add min sample size (we suggest >=2k requests per cohort) before enabling p95 regression gating; keep 5xx/timeout stop conditions enabled at tighter thresholds.\n\nAlso: This aligns with internal SRE guidance page on Hosted rollout SLO metrics/alerts (linked).",
    "2025-03-28 16:02 UTC \u2014 Dev Patel (Support): Internal note: filing feedback to product/eng to adjust beta defaults (sample-size gating + grace after step changes). Linking incident so this doesn\u2019t get mistaken for model regression.",
    "2025-04-01 17:31 UTC \u2014 Jordan Lee (Policy Engine): FYI we can enforce safer defaults via policy for beta tenants (min soak + max sensitivity). However, current UX still allows aggressive latency rule with short lookback. Suggest we update recommended preset in wizard and add warning copy when lookback <10m at <50% traffic.",
    "2025-04-02 09:08 UTC \u2014 Owen Phillips (Support): Customer confirmed rollout completed (100%) on 2025-03-28 with no further auto-pauses. Closing as resolved. Follow-up action tracked with product/eng separately (beta defaults + grace period + sample size gating)."
  ],
  "resolution": "Determined auto-pause was a false positive triggered by default p95 latency regression rule during a transient us-east latency incident affecting both cohorts, combined with a short evaluation window and low/uneven sample sizes immediately after a step change. Customer resumed rollout after the event cleared and completed rollout successfully.\n\nCustomer-facing outcome\n- Provided explanation with timestamps + cohort dashboard interpretation.\n- Recommended threshold tuning (longer lookback, higher regression threshold temporarily, minimum sample-size gating) for subsequent rollouts.\n\nInternal outcome\n- Captured beta feedback to adjust recommended wizard defaults and to add safeguards (sample size + grace period after step transitions) to reduce false pauses.",
  "next_steps": [
    "Product/Eng: Update rollout wizard recommended preset for latency stop conditions (lookback >=10m; guidance when <50% traffic).",
    "SRE/Telemetry: Add minimum sample-size gating for p95 regression evaluation and a grace period after step changes (beta hardening).",
    "Support: Add this scenario to canned responses / troubleshooting for \"rollout paused unexpectedly\" with links to cohort dashboards and the runbook."
  ],
  "title_field_name": "summary",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "comments",
    "resolution",
    "next_steps"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_dcdece5c12124b378e480e5c0d987a76"
}

# Hosted API launch readiness

Owner: Ethan Park, Platform & Console
Final recommendation: **NO-GO for external launch; continue internal dogfood only**

## Decision

Do not enable the planned Hosted API capability for design partners, a soft-launch cohort, or broad availability yet. Continue internal dogfood and preflight validation behind tenant and global kill switches. Reconsider a limited, allowlisted Hosted-only cohort only after every accepted criterion below has evidence and the named approvers sign the go/no-go record. No launch date is proposed.

The product is coherent and customer demand is validated, but external exposure is not supportable while security, billing, release, rollback, beta-exit, and support gates remain incomplete or unproven. This is a no-go, not a rejection of the capability.

## Supported eventual launch scope

When gates pass, the supported first external scope is Hosted routes only, per-tenant allowlisted: chat/completions with streaming, embeddings (single and batches up to 8), and dedicated-route rerank through a versioned REST/OpenAPI contract and core JS/Python SDKs. It requires tier-aware quotas, billing, OAuth2/API keys, retry guidance, deterministic cohorting, guardrails, audit history, cohort metrics, and baseline rollback. Dedicated/private deployments, full non-core SDK parity, time-based step scheduling, automated quality gates, and custom per-tenant runtime/quantization remain out of scope. Start with a design-partner cohort; broad availability is a separate decision.

[PM-80421; dsid_6f6a548d740249f6a1413a8ab778f270; /knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/PM-80421-hosted-api-capability-prioritization-acceptance-rollout.json] [dsid_fa0fb79e2f54457093ad3f831e7ac6a2; /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/hosted-canary-ga-change-management-checklist.json]

## Evidence supporting the capability

- The PRD defines the four endpoint families, compatibility rules, SLOs, telemetry, migration, and staged rollout.
- Six design partners used production rollouts. Four are recorded ready for GA and two conditional. Customers value percentage ramps, approval gates, metrics comparison, cohort stickiness, and rollback. Northstar’s how-to request closed after enablement and successful setup.
- The published SRE policy covers all four route families for paid multi-region-eligible Hosted traffic and defines a 99.95% rolling-30-day availability target plus actionable multi-window burn policy.
- Beta defects produced useful fixes and runbook requirements: the false-positive Northstar pause was resolved, and the split-mismatch mitigation was deployed before DocuSage completed its retry.

Customer/cohort: [dsid_22985fdc50d14444b0d278a5d93f5e08; /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/product/console-and-rollouts/beta-design-partners-tracker-hosted-canary.json]. Support: [SUP-48211; dsid_c67a7f60aa1b4f3c81e82921aa73610a; /knowledge/company/sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-48211-how-do-i-do-a-percentage-rollout-on-hosted-route.json] [SUP-48302; dsid_dcdece5c12124b378e480e5c0d987a76; /knowledge/company/sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-48302-rollout-paused-unexpectedly-after-latency-spike.json]. SRE: [dsid_4a94c098221d4588837f9949309656bc; /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/multi-region-availability-slo-2026.json].

## Launch blockers

1. **Security approval is absent.** The broader Hosted API threat model, penetration test, KMS/key-rotation E2E, RBAC, and audit verification are required; the safeguard-specific review is insufficient. Owner: Security.
2. **Billing is not ready.** Token accounting and plan enforcement are todo and explicitly gate GA. Owner: Billing Engineering.
3. **Release controls are not evidenced complete.** The release checklist remains in review with deployment, migration, monitoring, RBAC, docs, runbook, kill-switch, and final-signoff boxes unresolved. Owners: Connor O’Brien / Platform / Smart Routing / Console / Security.
4. **Stop/soak defaults are not accepted.** The release checklist still has blank thresholds, while beta evidence shows false pauses for bursty/low-sample traffic. Owners: Product / SRE / Telemetry.
5. **Rollback is not proven to acceptance.** ENG-87209 is In Progress; safe drain/KV-hot prioritization, automated rollback integration, DR rehearsal, and game-day proof remain. Owner: Liam O’Connor with SRE and Platform.
6. **Beta exit is not demonstrated.** PM-1859 requires at least 10 completed E2E rollouts and no open P0/P1 split, rollback, or audit gaps. The tracker shows six partners but does not demonstrate 10 completed rollouts; Emberfin remains conditional on audit schema/policy messaging and HelioTravel on threshold guidance. Owners: Marissa Cole / Simran Kaur / Security / Policy / SRE.
7. **Support readiness is not approved.** Evidence of two training sessions, sampled tickets resolved using final macros, finalized escalation SLA/channel, and support signoff is missing. Owner: Dev Patel / Support.
8. **Delivery/doc closure remains.** OpenAPI/examples, SDK RC1, performance report, randomized rerank E2E, migration/billing FAQ, streaming interruption states, and 24/72-hour staffing remain incomplete. Owners: Docs, SDK, Performance, QA, Design/Console, Observability.

Delivery: [PM-51555; dsid_ada92facaa334d3688c6a8371e0d001a; /knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/PM-51555-api-family-delivery-specification-chat-embeddings-rerank-launch-rundown.json]. Release: [dsid_fa0fb79e2f54457093ad3f831e7ac6a2; /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/hosted-canary-ga-change-management-checklist.json]. Rollback: [ENG-87209; dsid_a4b927b2fb2f45cb97bddda127a2cb37; /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-87209-hosted-api-regional-traffic-safeguard-playbook.json]. Beta exit: [PM-1859; dsid_5444ca17e9664747930ead86571d4804; /knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/PM-1859-ga-launch-criteria-and-beta-exit-checklist-hosted-canary.json].

## Accepted launch criteria for reconsideration

All criteria are mandatory for the first external allowlist:

- Product/API: frozen, published OpenAPI; JS/Python RCs; migration guide; streaming-interruption states; backward-compatibility tests; billing/quotas verified with test tenants.
- Security: documented approval for threat model, pen test with critical/major remediation, KMS rotation E2E, RBAC, complete audit-event identity/diffs/route and rollout IDs.
- Reliability: current error-budget state checked; Hosted multi-region target and burn alerts live; final sample-size, grace-period, threshold, and soak defaults signed by SRE; actionable cohort/region dashboards.
- Release: all required components deployed and verified; backward-compatible migration; three kill switches tested; no open launch-blocking severity issue; change record and on-call coverage prepared.
- Rollback: staging and internal-production E2E proves create/start/step/pause/rollback, forced breach, baseline restoration, audit visibility, and safe drain; tabletop/game day completed with owners and escalation path.
- Cohort: PM-1859 beta exit met, including at least 10 completed E2E rollouts, at least five enabled partners/three production users, no open P0/P1 split/rollback/audit gaps, and partner comprehension of state, next action, stop reason, and rollback.
- Support/docs: two support trainings with recording, final macros and troubleshooting for auto-pause/split mismatch/approval denial, sample-ticket validation, escalation SLA/channel, streaming/retry/stickiness guidance, limitations, and formal Support signoff.
- Approvals: Product, Engineering (Console/Control Plane/Smart Routing), SRE, Security, Release, and Support signatures recorded in the single go/no-go checklist.

## Evidence-backed next steps

- Marcus Lin / Security: close audit schema consistency and complete the Hosted API security package.
- Ben Carter / Billing Engineering: demonstrate token accounting and plan enforcement end to end.
- Sean Gallagher, Aisha Bello, Paula Mendes: ratify tier/traffic-volume threshold, minimum-sample, grace-period, and soak defaults using the resolved Northstar false-pause evidence.
- Liam O’Connor, SRE, Platform: finish ENG-87209 and run the rollback/game-day evidence path.
- Simran Kaur / Marissa Cole: reconcile the design-partner tracker against PM-1859 and record the required completed-rollout count and issue closure.
- Dev Patel / Support: run two trainings, validate final macros against representative tickets, publish escalation ownership, and sign readiness.
- Connor O’Brien: convene go/no-go only after the checklist contains evidence links and all required signatures; do not infer approval from ticket status.

## Final recommendation

**NO-GO for external launch. Internal dogfood may continue under existing controls.** The next eligible decision is a conditional-go for a Hosted-only, per-tenant allowlist after every accepted criterion above is evidenced; broad availability requires a later go/no-go.

## Accepted launch criteria for reconsideration

All criteria are mandatory for the first external allowlist:

- Product/API: frozen, published OpenAPI; JS/Python RCs; migration guide; streaming-interruption states; backward-compatibility tests; billing/quotas verified with test tenants.
- Security: documented approval for threat model, pen test with critical/major remediation, KMS rotation E2E, RBAC, complete audit-event identity/diffs/route and rollout IDs.
- Reliability: current error-budget state checked; Hosted multi-region target and burn alerts live; final sample-size, grace-period, threshold, and soak defaults signed by SRE; actionable cohort/region dashboards.
- Release: all required components deployed and verified; backward-compatible migration; three kill switches tested; no open launch-blocking severity issue; change record and on-call coverage prepared.
- Rollback: staging and internal-production E2E proves create/start/step/pause/rollback, forced breach, baseline restoration, audit visibility, and safe drain; tabletop/game day completed with owners and escalation path.
- Cohort: PM-1859 beta exit met, including at least 10 completed E2E rollouts, at least five enabled partners/three production users, no open P0/P1 split/rollback/audit gaps, and partner comprehension of state, next action, stop reason, and rollback.
- Support/docs: two support trainings with recording, final macros and troubleshooting for auto-pause/split mismatch/approval denial, sample-ticket validation, escalation SLA/channel, streaming/retry/stickiness guidance, limitations, and formal Support signoff.
- Approvals: Product, Engineering (Console/Control Plane/Smart Routing), SRE, Security, Release, and Support signatures recorded in the single go/no-go checklist.

## Evidence-backed next steps

- Marcus Lin / Security: close audit schema consistency and complete the Hosted API security package.
- Ben Carter / Billing Engineering: demonstrate token accounting and plan enforcement end to end.
- Sean Gallagher, Aisha Bello, Paula Mendes: ratify tier/traffic-volume threshold, minimum-sample, grace-period, and soak defaults using the resolved Northstar false-pause evidence.
- Liam O’Connor, SRE, Platform: finish ENG-87209 and run the rollback/game-day evidence path.
- Simran Kaur / Marissa Cole: reconcile the design-partner tracker against PM-1859 and record the required completed-rollout count and issue closure.
- Dev Patel / Support: run two trainings, validate final macros against representative tickets, publish escalation ownership, and sign readiness.
- Connor O’Brien: convene go/no-go only after the checklist contains evidence links and all required signatures; do not infer approval from ticket status.

## Final recommendation

**NO-GO for external launch. Internal dogfood may continue under existing controls.** The next eligible decision is a conditional-go for a Hosted-only, per-tenant allowlist after every accepted criterion above is evidenced; broad availability requires a later go/no-go.
